Emperor Wen: the Kaihuang code and statutes, the Three Departments and Six Ministries, the equal-field system with its grain and cloth taxes, the great census by physical inspection and the household registration reform; he abolished the Later Liang in 587 and conquered Chen in 589, ending nearly three hundred years of division between north and south.

units.note: 渤海高欢出身六镇怀朔镇，531 年在信都起兵讨尔朱氏，532 年韩陵大捷后立孝武帝，以晋阳为霸府遥控朝政；534 年另立孝静帝，迁都邺城（东魏），547 年死，子高澄、高洋相继执政。
units.notee: Gao Huan of Bohai came from Huaishuo, one of the Six Garrisons. In 531 he rose at Xindu against the Erzhu; after his great victory at Hanling in 532 he enthroned Emperor Xiaowu and controlled the court from afar through his headquarters at Jinyang. In 534 he set up Emperor Xiaojing instead and moved the capital to Ye (the Eastern Wei); he died in 547, and his sons Gao Cheng and Gao Yang held power after him.

units.note: 贺拔岳随尔朱天光平定关陇，尔朱氏败后统领关西；534 年被侯莫陈悦所杀，部将宇文泰接掌其众，迎孝武帝入关，开创西魏。
units.notee: Heba Yue helped Erzhu Tianguang pacify Guanlong, and after the fall of the Erzhu he commanded the west of the passes; in 534 he was killed by Houmochen Yue, and his general Yuwen Tai took over his army, welcomed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, and founded the Western Wei.

units.note: 秀容契胡酋长，以讨六镇余部起家。528 年以孝明帝暴死为由入洛，河阴之变屠杀王公朝臣，擒葛荣、平邢杲、败元颢，权倾朝野；530 年九月被孝庄帝手刃。
units.notee: A chieftain of the Qihu of Xiurong, he rose to power fighting the remnants of the Six Garrisons. In 528, citing the sudden death of Emperor Xiaoming, he entered Luoyang and massacred the princes and court officials at Heyin; he captured Ge Rong, put down Xing Gao and defeated Yuan Hao, dominating the court. In the 9th month of 530 he was killed by Emperor Xiaozhuang with his own hand.

units.note: 尔朱荣之侄，530 年攻入洛阳缢杀孝庄帝，据并州；532 年韩陵大败，533 年在秀容被高欢追及自杀。
units.notee: Nephew of Erzhu Rong. In 530 he broke into Luoyang, strangled Emperor Xiaozhuang and held Bing Province; routed at Hanling in 532, he was run down by Gao Huan at Xiurong in 533 and killed himself.

units.note: 尔朱荣从祖兄之子，530 年与贺拔岳、侯莫陈悦平定万俟丑奴，据关陇；532 年东出韩陵兵败，被高欢擒杀。
units.notee: Son of a second cousin of Erzhu Rong. In 530, with Heba Yue and Houmochen Yue, he put down Moqi Chounu and held Guanlong; in 532 he marched east and was defeated at Hanling, and was captured and killed by Gao Huan.

units.note: 尔朱荣从弟，530 年后为东南道大行台，据徐、兖二州，贪暴无度；532 年韩陵败后南奔梁。
units.notee: A cousin of Erzhu Rong. From 530 he was Grand Branch Department Director of the Southeast Circuit, holding Xu and Yan provinces, boundlessly greedy and cruel; after the defeat at Hanling in 532 he fled south to Liang.

units.note: 羯人侯景，原为尔朱荣部将，归高欢后任河南道大行台，拥兵十万，专制河南十四年。547 年高欢死后以河南十三州叛，先降西魏，再降梁。
units.notee: Hou Jing, a Jie, was originally a general of Erzhu Rong; after going over to Gao Huan he became Grand Branch Department Director of the Henan Circuit, commanding a hundred thousand troops and ruling Henan as he pleased for fourteen years. After Gao Huan's death in 547 he rebelled with thirteen provinces of Henan, submitting first to the Western Wei and then to Liang.

units.note: 沃野镇民，524 年杀镇将起兵，称真王，六镇响应，攻陷怀朔、武川诸镇；525 年被北魏与柔然阿那瓌联军击破，二十余万降户被安置河北。
units.notee: A garrison soldier of Woye, he killed the garrison commander in 524, rose in arms and took the title True King; the Six Garrisons rose in answer and Huaishuo, Wuchuan and the other garrisons fell. In 525 he was crushed by the combined armies of the Northern Wei and Anagui of the Rouran, and more than two hundred thousand of those who surrendered were resettled in Hebei.

units.note: 524 年秦州羌人莫折大提起兵，其子莫折念生继立称天子，据秦、陇诸州；527 年被部将杜粲所杀。
units.notee: In 524 Mozhe Dati, a Qiang of Qin Province, rose in arms; his son Mozhe Niansheng succeeded him, styled himself Son of Heaven and held the provinces of Qin and Long; in 527 he was killed by his general Du Can.

units.note: 高平敕勒人胡琛 524 年起兵，部将万俟丑奴继统其众，528 年称帝，据有关陇；530 年被尔朱天光、贺拔岳擒杀。
units.notee: Hu Chen, a Chile of Gaoping, rose in arms in 524; his general Moqi Chounu took over his followers, proclaimed himself emperor in 528 and held Guanlong; in 530 he was captured and killed by Erzhu Tianguang and Heba Yue.

units.note: 柔玄镇人，525 年在上谷起兵，据幽州；528 年被葛荣所并。
units.notee: A man of the Rouxuan Garrison, he rose at Shanggu in 525 and held You Province; in 528 his following was absorbed by Ge Rong.

units.note: 鲜于修礼部将，526 年继统其众，称帝，国号齐，并杜洛周，众号百万；528 年九月在滏口被尔朱荣以七千骑击破生擒。
units.notee: A general of Xianyu Xiuli, he took over his followers in 526, proclaimed himself emperor with the dynastic name Qi, absorbed Du Luozhou, and was said to command a million men; in the 9th month of 528 he was routed and captured at Fukou by Erzhu Rong with seven thousand horsemen.

units.note: 河间人，528 年率河北流民在青州北海起兵，称汉王；529 年被元天穆平定。
units.notee: A man of Hejian, he led refugees from Hebei in a rising at Beihai in Qing Province in 528 and styled himself King of Han; he was put down by Yuan Tianmu in 529.

units.note:
北齐营州刺史，齐亡后不降北周，据营州（今辽宁朝阳），联结突厥、契丹，拥戴流亡突厥的北齐宗室高绍义。
583 年隋军击败突厥后，高宝宁众叛亲离，为部下所杀。
units.notee:
Northern Qi prefect of Yingzhou; when Qi fell he refused to surrender to Northern Zhou, held Yingzhou (modern Chaoyang, Liaoning) and allied with the Turks and the Khitan, and upheld Gao Shaoyi of the Northern Qi imperial house, then in exile among the Turks.
In 583, after Sui forces defeated the Turks, Gao Baoning was deserted by his followers and kin and was killed by his own men.

units.note: 547 年以河南降梁，次年兵败涡阳，退据寿阳；548 年八月起兵反梁，十月渡江，549 年三月攻破台城，梁武帝饿死；551 年十一月称帝，国号汉。552 年三月被王僧辩、陈霸先击破，四月被部下所杀。
units.notee: In 547 Hou Jing surrendered to Liang with Henan; the next year he was defeated at Guoyang and fell back to hold Shouyang. In the 8th month of 548 he rose against Liang, crossed the Yangtze in the 10th month, and in the 3rd month of 549 he took Taicheng, where Emperor Wu of Liang starved to death; in the 11th month of 551 he proclaimed himself emperor, naming his state Han. In the 3rd month of 552 he was crushed by Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian, and in the 4th month he was killed by his own men.

units.note: 梁武帝第七子，镇江陵。侯景之乱时拥兵观望，先后攻杀萧誉、萧纶，552 年平定侯景后在江陵即位（梁元帝）；554 年江陵被西魏攻破，被杀。
units.notee: Seventh son of Emperor Wu of Liang, stationed at Jiangling. During Hou Jing's rebellion he held back his army and watched, attacking and killing Xiao Yu and Xiao Lun; after putting down Hou Jing in 552 he took the throne at Jiangling (Emperor Yuan of Liang). In 554 Jiangling was sacked by the Western Wei and he was killed.

units.note: 梁武帝第八子，镇益州十七年。552 年在成都称帝，率军东下攻萧绎，553 年兵败被杀，巴蜀被西魏乘虚夺取。
units.ne: Xiao Ji, Prince of Wuling (Yi Province)
units.notee: Eighth son of Emperor Wu of Liang, he governed Yi Province for seventeen years. In 552 he proclaimed himself emperor at Chengdu and led his army down the Yangtze against Xiao Yi; in 553 he was defeated and killed, and the Western Wei took the opportunity to seize Ba-Shu.

units.note: 梁武帝之孙，侯景之乱时任湘州刺史，与叔父萧绎相攻，550 年四月被杀。
units.ne: Xiao Yu, Prince of Hedong (Xiang Province)
units.notee: Grandson of Emperor Wu of Liang and Inspector of Xiang Province during Hou Jing's rebellion, he fought his uncle Xiao Yi and was killed in the 4th month of 550.

units.note: 萧誉之弟，镇襄阳，549 年为对抗萧绎称藩于西魏；554 年随西魏军攻破江陵，555 年称帝，即后梁。
units.notee: Younger brother of Xiao Yu, stationed at Xiangyang. In 549 he submitted to the Western Wei as a vassal in order to resist Xiao Yi; in 554 he joined the Western Wei army in sacking Jiangling, and in 555 he proclaimed himself emperor — the Later Liang.

units.note: 萧绎部将，551 年坚守巴陵挫败侯景，552 年攻入建康；555 年迎立北齐送回的萧渊明，九月被陈霸先袭杀。
units.notee: A general of Xiao Yi. In 551 he held Baling and thwarted Hou Jing, and in 552 he fought his way into Jiankang; in 555 he accepted Xiao Yuanming, sent back by Northern Qi, as emperor, and in the 9th month he was killed in a surprise attack by Chen Baxian.

units.note: 吴兴人，起家岭南，547 年平定交州李贲，551 年起兵讨侯景，552 年与王僧辩攻入建康，镇京口；555 年袭杀王僧辩，557 年代梁建陈。
units.notee: A man of Wuxing who rose to prominence in Lingnan. In 547 he put down Lý Bí in Jiao Province, in 551 he rose against Hou Jing, and in 552 he and Wang Sengbian fought their way into Jiankang, after which he was stationed at Jingkou; in 555 he killed Wang Sengbian in a surprise attack, and in 557 he replaced Liang and founded Chen.

units.note: 萧绎部将，镇湘州，拒不奉陈，558 年在郢州奉萧庄为梁帝，联结北齐；560 年二月在芜湖被侯瑱大败，投奔北齐，573 年在寿阳被陈军所杀。
units.notee: A general of Xiao Yi, stationed in Xiang Province, he refused to serve Chen. In 558 in Ying Province he set up Xiao Zhuang as emperor of Liang, allying himself with Northern Qi; in the 2nd month of 560 he was routed by Hou Tian at Wuhu and fled to Northern Qi, and in 573 he was killed by the Chen army at Shouyang.

units.note: 萧懿之弟，雍州刺史，镇襄阳。500 年十一月起兵讨东昏侯，联合荆州萧颖胄，奉南康王萧宝融，501 年十二月攻入建康，502 年代齐建梁。
units.ne: Xiao Yan (rising in Yong and Jing)
units.notee: Younger brother of Xiao Yi (萧懿) and Inspector of Yong Province, stationed at Xiangyang. In the 11th month of 500 he rose against the Marquis of Donghun, joined forces with Xiao Yingzhou in Jing Province and set up Xiao Baorong, Prince of Nankang; in the 12th month of 501 he fought his way into Jiankang, and in 502 he replaced Qi and founded Liang.

units.note:
萧詧 555 年在西魏扶植下据江陵称帝，史称后梁或西梁，为北周、隋附庸，疆域仅江陵一隅“方三百里”。
587 年隋文帝征后主萧琮入朝，废其国；萧琮之族子即后来起兵巴陵的萧铣。
units.notee:
Xiao Cha proclaimed himself emperor at Jiangling in 555 with Western Wei backing; known to history as Later Liang or Western Liang, it was a vassal of Northern Zhou and Sui, its territory confined to the area around Jiangling, "300 li square".
In 587 Emperor Wen of Sui summoned its Last Ruler, Xiao Cong, to court and abolished the state; Xiao Cong's clan nephew was Xiao Xian, who later rose in arms at Baling.

units.note:
交州豪族李贲 541 年起兵、544 年称帝（越南史称前李朝），547 年被梁将陈霸先击败；部将赵光复据夜泽坚持，550 年收复龙编，自称越王。571 年李佛子袭杀赵光复，据交州龙编一带，名义上奉南朝。
602 年隋以刘方为交州道行军总管，李佛子请降，被送往长安，交州归隋。
units.notee:
Lý Bí, of a great family of Jiao Province, rose in arms in 541 and proclaimed himself emperor in 544 (the Early Lý dynasty in Vietnamese history); in 547 he was defeated by the Liang general Chen Baxian. His general Triệu Quang Phục held out in the Dạ Trạch marshes, recovered Longbian in 550 and styled himself King of Yue. In 571 Lý Phật Tử killed Triệu Quang Phục in a surprise attack and held the area around Longbian in Jiao Province, nominally acknowledging the Southern Dynasties.
In 602 Sui made Liu Fang Expeditionary Commander of the Jiaozhou Route; Lý Phật Tử asked to surrender, was sent to Chang'an, and Jiaozhou passed to Sui.

units.note: 东胡之后。北匈奴西迁后鲜卑入居漠北，2 世纪中叶檀石槐统一诸部。三国后期拓跋、慕容、宇文、段、秃发、乞伏等部兴起，十六国时期多数南下建国；留在漠北者渐为柔然、敕勒所并。
units.notee: Descendants of the Donghu. After the Northern Xiongnu moved west, the Xianbei moved into the lands north of the Gobi, and in the mid-2nd century Tanshihuai united their tribes. In the late Three Kingdoms period the Tuoba, Murong, Yuwen, Duan, Tufa, Qifu and other tribes rose to prominence, and in the Sixteen Kingdoms period most of them moved south and founded states; those who stayed north of the Gobi were gradually absorbed by the Rouran and the Chile.

units.note: 东汉末年北地、上郡、朔方诸郡相继内徙，河套与鄂尔多斯一带不设郡县，羌、胡、匈奴杂居，西晋时仍为弃地。310 年后为铁弗匈奴所据。
units.notee: At the end of the Eastern Han the commanderies of Beidi, Shang and Shuofang were withdrawn inland one after another; the Hetao and the Ordos had no commanderies or counties and were home to a mix of Qiang, Hu and Xiongnu, and they were still abandoned lands under the Western Jin. After 310 they were held by the Tiefu Xiongnu.

units.note: 东胡后裔，原为拓跋鲜卑的附属部落。402 年社仑统一漠北，自称丘豆伐可汗，与北魏为世敌，北魏称之为“蠕蠕”。5 世纪时东至大兴安岭、西至焉耆，控制高昌。阿那瓌在 520 年代借北魏之助复国，541 年灭高车。552 年被突厥土门可汗攻灭，阿那瓌自杀。
units.notee: Descendants of the Donghu, originally a tribe subject to the Tuoba Xianbei. In 402 Shelun united the lands north of the Gobi and styled himself Qiudoufa Qaghan; the Rouran were the hereditary enemies of the Northern Wei, which called them "Ruanruan" (wriggling worms). In the 5th century their power reached the Greater Khingan in the east and Karasahr in the west, and they controlled Gaochang. Anagui restored the state with Northern Wei help in the 520s and destroyed the Gaoche in 541. In 552 the Rouran were destroyed by Tumen Qaghan of the Turks, and Anagui killed himself.

units.note: 又称敕勒、铁勒，因“车轮高大，辐数至多”得名，游牧于漠北。北魏多次掳掠其部众安置漠南，北朝民歌《敕勒歌》即咏其地。487 年副伏罗部阿伏至罗西迁，在车师前部西北建立高车国，541 年被柔然所灭。
units.notee: Also called Chile or Tiele, named for their carts "with tall wheels and very many spokes", they were nomads north of the Gobi. The Northern Wei repeatedly carried off their people and settled them south of the Gobi, and the Northern Dynasties folk song "Song of the Chile" celebrates that land. In 487 Afuzhiluo of the Fufuluo tribe moved west and founded the Gaoche kingdom northwest of Nearer Jushi, which was destroyed by the Rouran in 541.

units.note: 北匈奴西迁后留在龟兹以北的余部，5 世纪中叶据乌孙故地，436 年起多次遣使北魏，约共击柔然。
units.notee: Remnants of the Northern Xiongnu who stayed north of Kucha after the main body moved west. In the mid-5th century they held the former Wusun lands, and from 436 they repeatedly sent envoys to the Northern Wei, agreeing to attack the Rouran together.

units.note: 伊犁河流域的古国，汉代与汉朝和亲。4 世纪以后为柔然所逼，西迁葱岭山中。
units.notee: An ancient state in the Ili valley, which in Han times concluded marriage alliances with the Han. From the 4th century, pressed by the Rouran, the Wusun moved west into the Pamir mountains.

units.note:
突厥 552 年由阿史那土门建国，灭柔然，木杆可汗时东至辽海、西至西海（里海）。581 年隋立时可汗为沙钵略。
583 年隋分化突厥，沙钵略与阿波、达头反目，突厥分裂为东西两部。
units.notee:
The Turkic state was founded in 552 by Ashina Tumen, who destroyed the Rouran; under Muqan Qaghan it reached the Liao Sea in the east and the Western Sea (the Caspian) in the west. When Sui was founded in 581 the Qaghan was Ishbara.
In 583 Sui set the Turks against one another: Ishbara fell out with Apa and Tardu, and the Turks split into eastern and western halves.

units.note: 松花江流域的古国。285 年被慕容廆攻破，次年在晋的帮助下复国；346 年又被前燕所破，国王被俘；此后依附高句丽，494 年被勿吉所逼，王室投奔高句丽。
units.notee: An ancient state in the Songhua valley. It was crushed by Murong Hui in 285 and restored the following year with Jin help; in 346 it was crushed again by the Former Yan and its king captured. Thereafter it depended on Goguryeo; in 494, pressed by the Wuji, the royal house fled to Goguryeo.

units.note: 肃慎之后，居夫余东北的山林之中，善射，以楛矢石砮著称，曾向魏晋进贡。5 世纪改称勿吉。
units.notee: Descendants of the Sushen, living in the forests northeast of Buyeo; skilled archers famed for their hu-wood arrows with stone heads, they sent tribute to Wei and Jin. In the 5th century they came to be called Wuji.

units.note: 挹娄之后，5 世纪起见于史籍，475 年起遣使北魏，494 年逐夫余；6 世纪中叶改称靺鞨。
units.notee: Descendants of the Yilou, recorded from the 5th century; they sent envoys to the Northern Wei from 475 and drove out the Buyeo in 494, and in the mid-6th century came to be called Mohe.

units.note: 勿吉之后，分粟末、白山、黑水等七部，粟末靺鞨后来建立渤海国。
units.notee: Descendants of the Wuji, divided into seven tribes including the Sumo, Baishan and Heishui; the Sumo Mohe later founded the state of Balhae.

units.note: 又作失韦，北魏末年始与中原通使，居大兴安岭以北至嫩江、黑龙江一带，与契丹同源，语言相通。
units.notee: Also written Shiwei (失韦); they first exchanged envoys with the Central Plain at the end of the Northern Wei. They lived north of the Greater Khingan as far as the Nen and the Amur, shared their origins with the Khitan, and spoke a mutually intelligible language.

units.note: 鲜卑宇文部的余裔，344 年宇文部亡后散居松漠之间，388 年被北魏击破后与库莫奚分离，游牧于潢水（西拉木伦河）流域。
units.notee: Remnants of the Yuwen Xianbei. After the fall of the Yuwen in 344 they scattered across the Songmo region; after being crushed by the Northern Wei in 388 they separated from the Kumo Xi and roamed the valley of the Huang River (the Xar Moron).

units.note: 与契丹同出宇文部，388 年分离，居契丹西南，北魏称库莫奚，隋以后省称奚。
units.notee: They came from the Yuwen, like the Khitan, and separated from them in 388, living southwest of the Khitan; the Northern Wei called them Kumo Xi, and from Sui times they were called simply Xi.

units.note: 奚之北的游牧部落，6 世纪中叶起见于史籍，后称白霫。
units.notee: A nomadic tribe north of the Xi, recorded from the mid-6th century; later called the Bai Xi.

units.note: 青藏高原东缘与河湟的羌人部落，西晋时散居陇西、武都、河湟，十六国时为姚氏后秦的主力；高原腹地的发羌、唐旄诸部，后来融入吐蕃。
units.notee: Qiang tribes on the eastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau and in Hehuang. Under the Western Jin they lived scattered through Longxi, Wudu and Hehuang, and in the Sixteen Kingdoms period they were the main force of the Yao clan's Later Qin; the Fa Qiang, Tangmao and other tribes of the plateau interior were later absorbed into the Tibetan Empire.

units.note: 辽东鲜卑慕容部首领慕容廆之兄吐谷浑西迁，4 世纪初至枹罕，以甘松山、白兰为根据，329 年其孙叶延以祖名为国号。5 世纪据青海，431 年擒夏主赫连定；6 世纪夸吕称可汗，定都伏俟城，控制丝绸之路青海道。
units.notee: Tuyuhun, elder brother of Murong Hui, chief of the Murong Xianbei of Liaodong, moved west and reached Fuhan at the beginning of the 4th century, basing himself on Mount Gansong and Bailan; in 329 his grandson Yeyan made his grandfather's name the name of the state. In the 5th century the Tuyuhun held Qinghai, and in 431 they captured the Xia ruler Helian Ding; in the 6th century Kualü took the title Qaghan and made Fuqi City his capital, controlling the Qinghai route of the Silk Road.

units.note: 居青海西南（今都兰、玛多一带）的羌人部落，长期为吐谷浑的后方根据地，6 世纪中叶起单独见于史籍。
units.notee: A Qiang tribe in southwestern Qinghai (around today's Dulan and Madoi), long the rear base of the Tuyuhun; recorded separately from the mid-6th century.

units.note: 羌人的一支，以拓跋氏等八部为大，6 世纪后期见于史籍，居今青海东南、四川西北。
units.notee: A branch of the Qiang, among whose tribes eight were the strongest, the Tuoba among them; recorded from the late 6th century, they lived in today's southeastern Qinghai and northwestern Sichuan.

units.note: 川西高原的羌人诸部，《北史》《隋书》始有附国传，其南有东女国。
units.ne: Fuguo, Eastern Women's Kingdom and Qiang tribes
units.notee: Qiang tribes of the western Sichuan plateau; the History of the Northern Dynasties and the Book of Sui are the first to give an account of Fuguo, and south of it lay the Eastern Women's Kingdom.

units.note: 藏北的女王国，汉文史籍称“女国”“孙波”，7 世纪初被吐蕃征服。
units.notee: A kingdom ruled by queens in northern Tibet, called the "Women's Kingdom" and "Sunbo" in Chinese sources; conquered by the Tibetan Empire in the early 7th century.

units.note: 西藏西部的古国象雄，都穹窿银城，苯教发源地，644 年前后为吐蕃所灭。
units.notee: Zhangzhung, the ancient state of western Tibet, with its capital at Khyunglung Ngulkhar; birthplace of the Bon religion, it was destroyed by the Tibetan Empire around 644.

units.note: 雅隆河谷的悉补野部，6 世纪逐渐兼并邻部，7 世纪初松赞干布统一高原，建立吐蕃王朝。
units.notee: The Pugyal of the Yarlung valley gradually absorbed neighboring tribes in the 6th century, and in the early 7th century Songtsen Gampo united the plateau and founded the Tibetan Empire.

units.note: 东汉后期西域长史、戊己校尉时置时废，诸国互相兼并，以鄯善、于阗、龟兹、疏勒、焉耆为大。魏晋以西域长史驻楼兰海头，戊己校尉驻高昌，诸国名义附晋。
units.notee: In the late Eastern Han the posts of Chief Clerk of the Western Regions and Wuji Colonel were set up and abolished by turns, and the states swallowed one another, the largest being Shanshan, Khotan, Kucha, Kashgar and Karasahr. Under Wei and Jin the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions was stationed at Haitou in Loulan and the Wuji Colonel at Gaochang, and the states nominally submitted to Jin.

units.note: 楼兰故国，都扜泥，据罗布泊以西的丝路南道东段。魏晋时附中原，东晋十六国时附前凉、前秦；448 年被北魏万度归攻占，后入吐谷浑。
units.notee: The former state of Loulan, with its capital at Yuni, holding the eastern section of the southern Silk Road west of Lop Nur. It submitted to the Central Plain under Wei and Jin, and to the Former Liang and Former Qin in the Eastern Jin and Sixteen Kingdoms period; in 448 it was taken by Wan Dugui of the Northern Wei, and later passed to the Tuyuhun.

units.note: 吐鲁番盆地的古国，分前后部，前部都交河。450 年被北凉余部沮渠安周攻灭，地入高昌。
units.notee: An ancient state in the Turpan Basin, divided into Nearer and Further Jushi; the capital of Nearer Jushi was Jiaohe. In 450 it was destroyed by Juqu Anzhou of the Northern Liang remnants, and its land passed to Gaochang.

units.note: 西域中道古国，都员渠城，临博斯腾湖。448 年被北魏万度归攻破，此后附于柔然、高车、嚈哒、突厥。
units.notee: An ancient state on the middle route of the Western Regions, with its capital at Yuanqu City on Lake Bosten. In 448 it was taken by Wan Dugui of the Northern Wei; thereafter it submitted in turn to the Rouran, the Gaoche, the Hephthalites and the Turks.

units.note: 西域大国，都延城，佛教与音乐兴盛。384 年吕光攻破龟兹，掳鸠摩罗什东归；北朝时附于柔然、嚈哒，隋时附突厥。
units.notee: A great state of the Western Regions, with its capital at Yancheng, where Buddhism and music flourished. In 384 Lü Guang took Kucha and carried Kumarajiva back east; under the Northern Dynasties it submitted to the Rouran and the Hephthalites, and in Sui times to the Turks.

units.note: 丝路南道大国，崇奉大乘佛教，法显 401 年西行途经此地，称其“众僧数万人”。
units.notee: A great state on the southern Silk Road devoted to Mahayana Buddhism; Faxian passed through on his journey west in 401 and wrote that it had "tens of thousands of monks".

units.note: 西域西端的绿洲国家，扼葱岭东麓的商道。
units.notee: An oasis state at the western end of the Western Regions, commanding the trade routes at the eastern foot of the Pamirs.

units.note: 吐鲁番盆地的汉人城邦。魏晋为戊己校尉驻地，327 年前凉置高昌郡，442 年北凉余部沮渠无讳据此称王，460 年柔然立阚伯周为高昌王，此后历张、马二氏，498 年起麴氏为王，至 640 年。
units.notee: A Chinese city-state in the Turpan Basin. Under Wei and Jin it was the seat of the Wuji Colonel; the Former Liang set up Gaochang Commandery in 327; in 442 Juqu Wuhui of the Northern Liang remnants seized it and took the title of king; in 460 the Rouran made Kan Bozhou King of Gaochang, after whom the Zhang and Ma clans ruled in turn, and from 498 the Qu clan were kings until 640.

units.note: 锡尔河下游以北的游牧古国，魏晋时尚通使中原，其南的粟特诸城一度为其属国。
units.notee: An ancient nomadic state north of the lower Syr Darya; it still exchanged envoys with the Central Plain under Wei and Jin, and the Sogdian cities to its south were for a time its vassals.

units.note: 粟特诸城邦：康国（萨末建）、安国（布豁）、石国（赭时）、史国、米国等，善于经商，商队往来于中国与波斯之间。5 世纪末至 560 年代附于嚈哒，此后附于突厥。
units.notee: The Sogdian city-states — Kang (Samarkand), An (Bukhara), Shi (Chach), Shi (Kesh), Mi and others — gifted traders whose caravans went back and forth between China and Persia. From the late 5th century to the 560s they were subject to the Hephthalites, and thereafter to the Turks.

units.note: 费尔干纳盆地，汉代称大宛，北朝称破洛那、洛那，以汗血马著称。
units.notee: The Ferghana Valley, called Dayuan in Han times and Poluona or Luona under the Northern Dynasties, famous for its "blood-sweating" horses.

units.note: 阿姆河下游、咸海以南的绿洲国家，中国史籍称火寻、货利习弥。
units.notee: An oasis state on the lower Amu Darya south of the Aral Sea, called Huoxun and Huoliximi in Chinese sources.

units.note: 大月氏建立的帝国，2 世纪迦腻色伽王时极盛，3 世纪起被萨珊波斯夺去巴克特里亚，余部据犍陀罗、旁遮普，4 世纪中叶被寄多罗人取代。
units.notee: The empire founded by the Great Yuezhi, at its height under King Kanishka in the 2nd century; from the 3rd century Sasanian Persia took Bactria from it, its remnants held Gandhara and the Punjab, and in the mid-4th century it was replaced by the Kidarites.

units.note: 大月氏（贵霜）余部，4 世纪中叶由寄多罗率领南下，据有吐火罗、犍陀罗，自称贵霜后继者；5 世纪后期被嚈哒所逐。
units.notee: Remnants of the Great Yuezhi (Kushans) led south by Kidara in the mid-4th century; they held Tokharistan and Gandhara, called themselves heirs of the Kushans, and were driven out by the Hephthalites in the late 5th century.

units.note: 5 世纪中叶兴起于吐火罗的游牧民族，484 年击杀萨珊王卑路斯，此后萨珊向其纳贡；6 世纪初极盛，据有吐火罗、粟特、犍陀罗，役属西域诸国，其王摩醯逻矩罗南侵天竺。516 年前后遣使北魏、梁。约 560 年被突厥与萨珊夹击灭亡。
units.notee: A nomadic people who rose in Tokharistan in the mid-5th century. In 484 they killed the Sasanian king Peroz, and Persia paid them tribute thereafter; at their height in the early 6th century they held Tokharistan, Sogdiana and Gandhara and made the states of the Western Regions their subjects, and their king Mihirakula invaded India. Around 516 they sent envoys to the Northern Wei and to Liang. Around 560 they were crushed between the Turks and the Sasanians and destroyed.

units.note: 阿姆河上游的巴克特里亚地区，嚈哒亡后分为二十余小国，叶护牙帐设于活国，附于西突厥。
units.notee: Bactria on the upper Amu Darya. After the fall of the Hephthalites it broke up into more than twenty small states; the Yabghu's royal camp was at Huo (Warwaliz, near Kunduz), and the region was subject to the Western Turks.

units.note: 印度诸国的总称。笈多王朝以外，南有跋罗婆、伐迦陀迦等国；6 世纪中叶笈多瓦解后，北天竺有穆克里、后期笈多诸王，西有伐腊毗，德干有遮娄其，诸国并立，中国史籍称“五天竺”。
units.notee: The general name for the states of India. Besides the Gupta Empire there were the Pallavas, the Vakatakas and others in the south; after the Gupta Empire disintegrated in the mid-6th century the Maukharis and the later Guptas ruled in northern India, Valabhi in the west and the Chalukyas in the Deccan — states standing side by side, which Chinese sources called the "Five Indias".

units.note: 320 年旃陀罗笈多一世在摩揭陀创立，都华氏城。沙摩陀罗笈多（约 335—375）南征北讨，统一恒河流域；旃陀罗笈多二世（超日王，约 375—415）征服西方的塞种诸王，法显约 402—409 年在其境内游学。5 世纪后期起屡遭嚈哒入侵，6 世纪中叶瓦解。
units.notee: Founded in Magadha in 320 by Chandragupta I, with its capital at Pataliputra. Samudragupta (c. 335–375) campaigned in every direction and united the Ganges valley; Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya, c. 375–415) conquered the Saka kings of the west, and Faxian studied in his realm from about 402 to 409. From the late 5th century the empire suffered repeated Hephthalite invasions, and it disintegrated in the mid-6th century.

units.note: 克什米尔谷地，罽宾之东，佛教说一切有部的重镇，6 世纪初为嚈哒王摩醯逻矩罗所据。
units.notee: The Kashmir valley, east of Jibin, a stronghold of the Sarvastivada school of Buddhism; in the early 6th century it was seized by the Hephthalite king Mihirakula.

units.note: 喜马拉雅山南的尼泊尔谷地，离车毗王朝在 5 世纪兴起，都加德满都一带。
units.notee: The Kathmandu valley south of the Himalaya; the Licchavi dynasty rose in the 5th century, with its capital in the Kathmandu area.

units.note: 今斯里兰卡，佛教兴盛，都阿㝹罗陀补罗。法显 410—411 年在此留居两年，取得《五分律》等经典；东晋、宋、梁时多次遣使中国。
units.notee: Today's Sri Lanka, where Buddhism flourished, with its capital at Anuradhapura. Faxian stayed here for two years in 410–411 and obtained the Mahishasaka Vinaya and other scriptures; it sent envoys to China several times under the Eastern Jin, Song and Liang.

units.note: 192 年日南郡象林县人区连杀县令自立为王，建国林邑（即后来的占婆），此后屡侵日南、九真，347 年攻陷日南郡，据有其北部。605 年被隋将刘方攻破。
units.notee: In 192 Ou Lian of Xianglin County in Rinan Commandery killed the county magistrate and made himself king, founding Linyi (later Champa); thereafter it repeatedly raided Rinan and Jiuzhen, and in 347 it took Rinan Commandery and held its northern part. In 605 it was crushed by the Sui general Liu Fang.

units.note: 湄公河下游的古国，都特牧城，3 世纪范蔓时称霸中南半岛，役属顿逊等国，海上贸易繁盛；南朝时多次遣使，梁武帝时献佛发、珊瑚佛像。6 世纪中叶起被属国真腊侵逼。
units.notee: An ancient state on the lower Mekong, with its capital at Vyadhapura. In the 3rd century, under Fan Man, it dominated the Indochinese peninsula, made Dunxun and other states its subjects, and grew rich on maritime trade; under the Southern Dynasties it sent envoys many times, presenting a hair of the Buddha and a coral Buddha image to Emperor Wu of Liang. From the mid-6th century it was pressed by its vassal Chenla.

units.note: 原为扶南属国，6 世纪中叶起兼并扶南，都伊奢那城。
units.notee: Originally a vassal of Funan, from the mid-6th century it absorbed Funan, with its capital at Ishanapura.

units.note: 孟人在湄南河下游建立的国家，以佛统为中心，6—7 世纪兴起。
units.notee: A state founded by the Mon on the lower Chao Phraya, centered on Nakhon Pathom, rising in the 6th–7th centuries.

units.note: 缅甸伊洛瓦底江流域的骠人城邦，都室利差呾罗。
units.notee: The Pyu city-states of the Irrawaddy valley in Myanmar, with their capital at Sri Ksetra.

units.note: 马来半岛北部的古国，宋、梁时多次遣使，献佛牙、画塔。
units.notee: An ancient state in the northern Malay Peninsula that sent envoys many times under Song and Liang, presenting a Buddha's tooth and painted stupas.

units.note: 马来半岛中部的古国，515 年起遣使于梁，《梁书》载其“累砖为城，重门楼阁”。
units.notee: An ancient state in the central Malay Peninsula that sent envoys to Liang from 515; the Book of Liang records that its people "pile up bricks to make walls, with double gates and towers".

units.note: 马来半岛东岸的古国，梁中大通、大同年间遣使献牙像、牙塔。
units.notee: An ancient state on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula that sent envoys in the Zhongdatong and Datong eras of Liang, presenting ivory images and ivory stupas.

units.note: 马来半岛南部（今彭亨一带）的古国，宋元嘉年间遣使。
units.notee: An ancient state in the southern Malay Peninsula (around today's Pahang) that sent envoys in the Yuanjia era of Song.

units.note: 南海古国，地望说法不一，多认为在苏门答腊东南（今巨港一带），宋、梁时遣使献金银、宝器。
units.notee: An ancient state of the Southern Seas whose location is disputed, though it is usually placed in southeastern Sumatra (around today's Palembang); it sent envoys under Song and Liang, presenting gold, silver and precious objects.

units.note: 西爪哇的古国，碑铭称多罗磨那加拉，5—7 世纪兴盛，奉印度教。
units.notee: An ancient state in West Java, called Tarumanagara in its inscriptions, which flourished from the 5th to the 7th century and followed Hinduism.

units.note: 爪哇的古国，宋元嘉年间（430—452）多次遣使。
units.notee: An ancient state on Java that sent envoys several times in the Yuanjia era of Song (430–452).

units.note: 南海岛国，518 年遣使于梁，地望一说为巴厘岛，一说在加里曼丹。
units.notee: An island state of the Southern Seas that sent envoys to Liang in 518; it is placed by some on Bali and by others on Kalimantan.

units.note: 建国于浑江、鸭绿江中游，都丸都（国内城）。313、314 年攻灭乐浪、带方二郡；342 年被前燕攻破丸都，371 年被百济攻杀故国原王。广开土王（391—412）大举拓地，取后燕辽东；长寿王 427 年迁都平壤，475 年攻陷百济汉城，疆域达于极盛。
units.notee: Founded on the middle Hun and Yalu rivers, with its capital at Hwando (Gungnae Fortress). In 313 and 314 it destroyed Lelang and Daifang commanderies; in 342 the Former Yan sacked Hwando, and in 371 Baekje killed King Gogugwon. King Gwanggaeto (391–412) expanded greatly, taking Liaodong from the Later Yan; King Jangsu moved the capital to Pyongyang in 427 and in 475 took Hanseong, the Baekje capital, bringing the kingdom to its greatest extent.

units.note: 马韩伯济国发展而成，都汉城（慰礼城），近肖古王（346—375）时尽并马韩、北攻平壤；475 年汉城被高句丽攻陷，迁都熊津，538 年迁泗沘。与倭国关系密切，曾传儒学、佛教于倭。
units.notee: Grew out of the state of Baekje (伯济) in Mahan, with its capital at Hanseong (Wiryeseong). Under King Geunchogo (346–375) it absorbed all of Mahan and attacked Pyongyang to the north; in 475 Hanseong fell to Goguryeo and the capital moved to Ungjin, and in 538 to Sabi. Closely linked with Wa, it passed Confucian learning and Buddhism on to Wa.

units.note: 由辰韩斯卢国发展而成，都金城（今庆州）。奈勿王（356—402）时统合辰韩，智证王时定国号新罗，法兴王 532 年并金官伽倻，真兴王 551—553 年夺取汉江流域，562 年灭大伽倻。
units.notee: Grew out of the state of Saro in Jinhan, with its capital at Geumseong (today's Gyeongju). Under King Naemul (356–402) it united Jinhan; King Jijeung fixed the name Silla; King Beopheung annexed Geumgwan Gaya in 532; King Jinheung seized the Han River basin in 551–553 and destroyed Daegaya in 562.

units.note: 朝鲜半岛西南部的五十余小国，4 世纪中叶起被其中的伯济国（百济）统一。
units.notee: More than fifty small states in southwestern Korea, united from the mid-4th century by one of them, Baekje (伯济).

units.note: 朝鲜半岛东南部的十二国，其中的斯卢国 4 世纪发展为新罗。
units.notee: Twelve states in southeastern Korea, one of which, Saro, grew into Silla in the 4th century.

units.note: 弁韩故地的金官、大伽倻、阿罗等小国联盟，铁器发达，与倭国往来频繁；532 年金官、562 年大伽倻相继并入新罗。
units.notee: A league of small states in the former Byeonhan lands — Geumgwan, Daegaya, Ara and others — advanced in ironworking and in close contact with Wa; Geumgwan was annexed by Silla in 532 and Daegaya in 562.

units.note: 日本列岛。3 世纪有邪马台国女王卑弥呼，266 年台与遣使西晋；5 世纪“倭五王”赞、珍、济、兴、武相继遣使南朝宋，求封“安东大将军、倭国王”；6 世纪末推古天皇以飞鸟为都。
units.notee: The Japanese archipelago. In the 3rd century there was Himiko, queen of Yamatai, and in 266 Toyo sent envoys to the Western Jin; in the 5th century the "Five Kings of Wa" — San, Chin, Sei, Kō and Bu — sent envoys in turn to Liu Song, seeking the titles "Grand General Who Pacifies the East, King of Wa"; at the end of the 6th century Empress Suiko made Asuka her capital.

units.note: 萨珊王朝（224—651），都泰西封，奉祆教。沙普尔二世（309—379）击败罗马皇帝尤利安，夺回尼西比斯；卑路斯 484 年被嚈哒击杀，此后纳贡嚈哒数十年；库思老一世（531—579）改革税制，与西突厥合灭嚈哒，570 年出兵也门。北魏、梁时多次遣使中国。
units.notee: The Sasanian dynasty (224–651), with its capital at Ctesiphon, following Zoroastrianism. Shapur II (309–379) defeated the Roman emperor Julian and recovered Nisibis; Peroz was killed by the Hephthalites in 484, after which Persia paid them tribute for decades; Khosrow I (531–579) reformed taxation, destroyed the Hephthalites together with the Western Turks, and sent an army to Yemen in 570. Persia sent envoys to China many times under the Northern Wei and Liang.

units.note: 中国史籍所称的大秦。戴克里先（284—305）推行四帝共治，君士坦丁 330 年迁都君士坦丁堡；395 年帝国分为东西，西罗马 476 年灭亡，东罗马（拜占庭）延续。查士丁尼（527—565）时收复北非、意大利，与萨珊长期争夺亚美尼亚与美索不达米亚；约 550 年僧侣将蚕种带回君士坦丁堡。284 年大秦遣使西晋，《魏书》所载“普岚”使者一说即东罗马。
units.notee: The Daqin of Chinese sources. Diocletian (284–305) introduced the Tetrarchy, and Constantine moved the capital to Constantinople in 330; in 395 the empire was divided into East and West, the Western Roman Empire fell in 476, and the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire continued. Under Justinian (527–565) it recovered North Africa and Italy and fought the Sasanians at length over Armenia and Mesopotamia; around 550 monks brought silkworm eggs back to Constantinople. In 284 Daqin sent envoys to the Western Jin, and the "Pulan" envoys recorded in the Book of Wei are thought by some to have come from the Eastern Roman Empire.

units.note: 罗马与波斯之间的王国，301 年前后以基督教为国教。387 年被两国瓜分，罗马得西部，波斯得东部五分之四；428 年萨珊废其国王，改设总督。
units.notee: A kingdom between Rome and Persia that made Christianity its state religion around 301. In 387 it was partitioned between the two empires, Rome taking the west and Persia the eastern four-fifths; in 428 the Sasanians deposed its king and installed a governor.

units.note: 高加索南麓的古国（今格鲁吉亚东部），4 世纪皈依基督教，在罗马与萨珊之间摇摆，约 580 年王权被萨珊废除。
units.notee: An ancient state on the southern slopes of the Caucasus (today's eastern Georgia) that converted to Christianity in the 4th century and wavered between Rome and the Sasanians; its monarchy was abolished by the Sasanians around 580.

units.note: 里海西岸、库拉河下游的古国（今阿塞拜疆），长期依附萨珊；萨珊在其北境修筑杰尔宾特关城，防御北方草原诸族。
units.notee: An ancient state on the west shore of the Caspian and the lower Kura (today's Azerbaijan), long dependent on the Sasanians, who built the fortress of Derbent on its northern border against the peoples of the northern steppe.

units.note: 以希拉为中心的阿拉伯王国，萨珊的附庸，替萨珊防守沙漠边境，与东罗马的盟邦加萨尼对峙。
units.notee: An Arab kingdom centered on Hira, a Sasanian client that guarded the desert frontier for the Sasanians and faced the Ghassanids, allies of the Eastern Roman Empire.

units.note: 叙利亚边地的阿拉伯部落联盟，502 年起成为东罗马的盟邦，信奉基督教一性论派。
units.notee: An Arab tribal confederation on the Syrian frontier, allied with the Eastern Roman Empire from 502, following Miaphysite Christianity.

units.note: 阿拉伯半岛的游牧与绿洲部落，麦加为商队贸易中心；570 年前后穆罕默德生于麦加。
units.notee: The nomadic and oasis tribes of the Arabian Peninsula, with Mecca as a center of the caravan trade; Muhammad was born in Mecca around 570.

units.note: 也门的古国，约 3 世纪末统一南阿拉伯，控制红海、印度洋的香料贸易；525 年被阿克苏姆攻灭。
units.notee: An ancient state in Yemen that united South Arabia around the end of the 3rd century and controlled the spice trade of the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean; it was destroyed by Aksum in 525.

units.note: 今埃塞俄比亚的基督教王国，525 年渡红海攻灭希木叶尔，扶植阿布拉哈统治也门；570 年前后被萨珊逐出。
units.notee: A Christian kingdom in today's Ethiopia that crossed the Red Sea in 525 to destroy Himyar and set up Abraha to rule Yemen; it was driven out by the Sasanians around 570.

units.note: 伊朗语族游牧民，汉代称奄蔡，《后汉书》载“奄蔡国改名阿兰聊”，居里海、黑海以北草原；375 年前后被匈人击破，一部西迁。
units.notee: Iranian-speaking nomads, called Yancai in Han times — the Book of the Later Han records that "Yancai has changed its name to Alanliao" — living on the steppe north of the Caspian and the Black Sea; around 375 they were crushed by the Huns, and some of them moved west.

units.note: 日耳曼部落，3—4 世纪居黑海北岸，建立东哥特王国；375 年前后被匈人击破，西哥特部落 376 年渡多瑙河进入罗马境内。
units.notee: Germanic tribes who lived on the north shore of the Black Sea in the 3rd–4th centuries, where the Ostrogothic kingdom arose; around 375 they were crushed by the Huns, and in 376 the Visigothic tribes crossed the Danube into Roman territory.

units.note: 4 世纪后期自伏尔加河以东西进的游牧民，击破阿兰、哥特，5 世纪中叶阿提拉时建立横跨中欧的帝国，453 年阿提拉死后瓦解。其与匈奴的关系，学界仍有争论。
units.notee: Nomads who moved west from beyond the Volga in the late 4th century, crushing the Alans and the Goths; in the mid-5th century under Attila they built an empire spanning central Europe, which broke up after Attila died in 453. Their relationship to the Xiongnu is still debated by scholars.

units.note: 匈人瓦解后黑海、里海以北草原上的突厥语游牧部落，萨比尔人曾为东罗马、萨珊雇佣。
units.notee: Turkic-speaking nomadic tribes on the steppe north of the Black Sea and the Caspian after the Hunnic empire broke up; the Sabirs served as mercenaries of both the Eastern Roman Empire and the Sasanians.

units.note: 约 557 年自东方迁至黑海北岸草原的游牧民，东罗马史家认为其与柔然有关，568 年西迁潘诺尼亚。
units.notee: Nomads who arrived on the steppe north of the Black Sea from the east around 557 — Eastern Roman historians linked them with the Rouran — and moved west to Pannonia in 568.

units.note: 南中大姓，两晋以来世为宁州豪族，梁末以后据南宁州（今曲靖）一带称雄，名义上奉中原。
units.notee: A great clan of Nanzhong, hereditary magnates of Ning Province from the Jin period; from the end of Liang they dominated the area of Nanning Province (today's Qujing), nominally acknowledging the Central Plain.

units.note: 洱海周边的乌蛮、白蛮诸部，后来形成六诏，738 年南诏统一。
units.notee: The Wuman and Baiman tribes around Erhai Lake, which later formed the Six Zhao and were united by Nanzhao in 738.

units.note: 黔中北部的诸蛮部落，以谢氏为首领。
units.notee: The tribes of the northern Qianzhong, led by the Xie clan.

items.mod: 河南洛阳东（汉魏洛阳故城）
items.note: 西晋都城，宫城在北，太极殿为正殿，城西北隅有金墉城。311 年六月被汉军攻破，宫室焚毁，怀帝被俘。

e.mod: east of Luoyang, Henan (Han–Wei Luoyang city site)
e.note: Capital of the Western Jin, with the palace city in the north, the Hall of Supreme Ultimate as its main hall, and Jinyong City in the northwest corner. In the 6th month of 311 it was taken by the Han army, the palaces were burned, and Emperor Huai was captured.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 313 年愍帝在长安即位，“户不盈百，蒿棘成林，公私有车四乘”；316 年十一月刘曜破城，愍帝出降。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
e.note: Emperor Min took the throne at Chang'an in 313, when "there were fewer than a hundred households, thorns and brambles grew like forests, and there were four carriages in all, public and private"; in the 11th month of 316 Liu Yao took the city and Emperor Min surrendered.

items.note: 孙吴建业，313 年避愍帝讳改名建康。317 年司马睿在此称晋王，东晋、宋、齐、梁、陈相继建都，史称六朝古都；宫城称台城，西有石头城，北临玄武湖。

e.note: Jianye of Sun Wu, renamed Jiankang in 313 to avoid the personal name of Emperor Min. Sima Rui took the title King of Jin here in 317, and the Eastern Jin, Song, Qi, Liang and Chen made it their capital in turn — known as the ancient capital of the Six Dynasties; the palace city was called Taicheng, with Shitou City to the west and Xuanwu Lake to the north.

items.note: 403 年十二月桓玄在此称帝，次年二月刘裕起兵后弃城西逃。

e.note: Huan Xuan proclaimed himself emperor here in the 12th month of 403, and abandoned the city and fled west after Liu Yu rose in the 2nd month of the following year.

items.note: 刘宋都城。

e.note: Capital of Liu Song.

items.note: 南齐都城。

e.note: Capital of Southern Qi.

items.note: 梁都城。549 年三月台城被侯景攻破；552 年元帝在江陵即位，不还建康；555 年敬帝在建康即位。

e.note: Capital of Liang. Taicheng fell to Hou Jing in the 3rd month of 549; in 552 Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jiangling and did not return to Jiankang; in 555 Emperor Jing took the throne at Jiankang.

items.note: 549 年侯景攻破台城后挟持简文帝，551 年十一月在此称帝，国号汉。

e.note: After taking Taicheng in 549 Hou Jing held Emperor Jianwen captive, and in the 11th month of 551 he proclaimed himself emperor here, naming his state Han.

items.note: 552 年十一月梁元帝萧绎在江陵即位，554 年十一月被西魏攻破。

e.note: Emperor Yuan of Liang, Xiao Yi, took the throne at Jiangling in the 11th month of 552; it was taken by the Western Wei in the 11th month of 554.

items.note: 陈都城，589 年正月被隋军攻破。

e.note: Capital of Chen, taken by the Sui army in the 1st month of 589.

items.note: 后梁（西梁）都城，萧氏三代据此为西魏、北周、隋附庸，587 年被废。

e.note: Capital of the Later Liang (Western Liang), where three generations of the Xiao ruled as vassals of the Western Wei, Northern Zhou and Sui; abolished in 587.

items.note: 南匈奴左部帅驻地。304 年十月刘渊在此称汉王，次年因饥荒南迁黎亭。

e.note: Seat of the commander of the Left Division of the Southern Xiongnu. Liu Yuan proclaimed himself King of Han here in the 10th month of 304, and the following year moved south to Liting because of famine.

items.note: 308 年十月刘渊在此即皇帝位，次年正月迁都平阳。

e.note: Liu Yuan took the imperial throne here in the 10th month of 308, and moved his capital to Pingyang in the 1st month of the following year.

items.note: 汉都城。311 年俘晋怀帝、316 年俘愍帝，皆送平阳；318 年靳准之乱后被石勒焚毁。

e.note: Capital of Han. Emperor Huai of Jin, captured in 311, and Emperor Min, captured in 316, were both sent to Pingyang; after Jin Zhun's coup of 318 it was burned by Shi Le.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 318 年十月刘曜即位，次年迁都长安，改国号赵（前赵）。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
e.note: Liu Yao took the throne in the 10th month of 318 and the following year moved his capital to Chang'an, renaming his state Zhao (Former Zhao).

items.note: 李雄 303 年攻占成都，304 年称成都王，306 年称帝；347 年三月桓温破城，李势出降。

e.note: Li Xiong took Chengdu in 303, proclaimed himself King of Chengdu in 304 and emperor in 306; in the 3rd month of 347 Huan Wen took the city and Li Shi surrendered.

items.note: 312 年石勒据为根据地，319 年在此称赵王，330 年称帝。

e.note: Shi Le made it his base in 312, proclaimed himself King of Zhao here in 319 and emperor in 330.

items.note: 335 年石虎迁都于邺，大兴宫室，起太武殿、东西宫，役使数十万人。

e.note: Shi Hu moved the capital to Ye in 335 and built palaces on a grand scale, raising the Taiwu Hall and the Eastern and Western Palaces with the labor of hundreds of thousands.

items.note: 350 年石祗在襄国称帝，次年被部将刘显所杀，后赵亡。

e.note: Shi Zhi proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo in 350 and was killed by his general Liu Xian the following year, and the Later Zhao came to an end.

items.note: 冉魏都城，352 年八月被前燕攻破。

e.note: Capital of Ran Wei, taken by the Former Yan in the 8th month of 352.

items.note: 前凉都城，张轨修筑，城有五城，中城为宫。

e.note: Capital of the Former Liang, built up by Zhang Gui; it consisted of five walled towns, the central one being the palace.

items.mod: 内蒙古和林格尔土城子
items.note: 拓跋代国北都，313 年猗卢所定（315 年称代王），什翼犍 341 年筑盛乐新城。

e.note: Northern capital of the Tuoba state of Dai, fixed by Yilu in 313 (he took the title King of Dai in 315); Shiyijian built the new city of Shengle in 341.

items.mod: 内蒙古和林格尔土城子
items.note: 258 年拓跋力微迁居定襄盛乐，此后为拓跋部中心。

e.note: Tuoba Liwei moved to Shengle in Dingxiang in 258, and thereafter it was the center of the Tuoba.

items.note: 294 年慕容廆移居大棘城，教民农桑，招徕中原流民。

e.note: Murong Hui moved to Daji City in 294, taught his people farming and sericulture, and drew in refugees from the Central Plain.

items.note: 337 年慕容皝在此称燕王，338 年后赵石虎围城十余日不克。

e.note: Murong Huang took the title King of Yan here in 337; in 338 Shi Hu of the Later Zhao besieged the city for more than ten days without taking it.

items.note: 341 年慕容皝在柳城之北筑城，称龙城，次年迁都；后燕、北燕亦都于此。

e.note: In 341 Murong Huang built a city north of Liucheng, called Longcheng, and moved his capital there the following year; the Later Yan and Northern Yan also had their capitals here.

items.note: 350 年前燕攻取蓟城，迁都于此，352 年慕容儁在此称帝。

e.note: The Former Yan took Ji City in 350 and moved its capital there; Murong Jun proclaimed himself emperor here in 352.

items.note: 357 年前燕迁都于邺，370 年十一月被前秦王猛攻破。

e.note: The Former Yan moved its capital to Ye in 357; it was taken by Wang Meng of the Former Qin in the 11th month of 370.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 前秦都城。苻坚时“关陇清晏，百姓丰乐”，自长安至诸州夹路树槐柳。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
e.note: Capital of the Former Qin. Under Fu Jian (苻坚) "Guanlong was at peace and the people prosperous and happy", and the roads from Chang'an to the provinces were lined with pagoda trees and willows.

items.note: 385 年苻丕放弃邺城，西走晋阳称帝。

e.note: In 385 Fu Pi abandoned Ye, went west to Jinyang and proclaimed himself emperor.

items.note: 386 年慕容垂在中山称帝，397 年三月慕容宝弃城北走。

e.note: Murong Chui proclaimed himself emperor at Zhongshan in 386; Murong Bao abandoned the city and went north in the 3rd month of 397.

items.note: 397 年后燕北退龙城，407 年慕容熙被杀于此。

e.note: The Later Yan fell back north to Longcheng in 397, and Murong Xi was killed here in 407.

items.note: 北燕都城，冯跋时“劝课农桑，轻徭薄赋”；436 年冯弘焚宫东奔高句丽。

e.note: Capital of the Northern Yan; Feng Ba "encouraged farming and sericulture and lightened labor service and taxes". In 436 Feng Hong burned the palaces and fled east to Goguryeo.

items.note: 386 年十月慕容永在此称帝，394 年八月被后燕攻破。

e.note: Murong Yong proclaimed himself emperor here in the 10th month of 386; it was taken by the Later Yan in the 8th month of 394.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 385 年五月慕容冲攻入长安，纵兵大掠；次年部众东归。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
e.note: Murong Chong broke into Chang'an in the 5th month of 385 and let his troops plunder at will; his people went back east the following year.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 后秦都城。401 年姚兴迎鸠摩罗什至长安，在逍遥园西明阁译经三百余卷。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
e.note: Capital of the Later Qin. In 401 Yao Xing brought Kumarajiva to Chang'an, where he translated more than three hundred scrolls of scripture in the Ximing Pavilion of the Xiaoyao Garden.

items.note: 乞伏国仁 385 年在苑川勇士城自称大单于，为西秦发祥之地。

e.note: Qifu Guoren styled himself Grand Chanyu at Yongshi City in Yuanchuan in 385; it was the birthplace of the Western Qin.

items.note: 388 年乞伏乾归迁都金城。

e.note: Qifu Gangui moved his capital to Jincheng in 388.

items.note: 412 年乞伏炽磐迁都枹罕。

e.note: Qifu Chipan moved his capital to Fuhan in 412.

items.note: 385 年吕光东归入姑臧，403 年八月吕隆东迁长安。

e.note: Lü Guang returned east and entered Guzang in 385; Lü Long moved east to Chang'an in the 8th month of 403.

items.note: 南凉都城，414 年被西秦袭破。

e.note: Capital of the Southern Liang, taken in a surprise attack by the Western Qin in 414.

items.note: 406 年后秦以姑臧授秃发傉檀，410 年败于北凉后退回乐都。

e.note: In 406 the Later Qin gave Guzang to Tufa Rutan, who fell back to Ledu after his defeat by the Northern Liang in 410.

items.note: 398 年段业取张掖为都，401 年沮渠蒙逊杀段业于此。

e.note: Duan Ye took Zhangye and made it his capital in 398; Juqu Mengxun killed Duan Ye here in 401.

items.note: 412 年沮渠蒙逊迁都姑臧，称河西王；439 年九月城破，北凉亡。

e.note: Juqu Mengxun moved his capital to Guzang in 412 and took the title King of Hexi; the city fell in the 9th month of 439, and the Northern Liang came to an end.

items.note: 442 年沮渠无讳据高昌称凉王，460 年被柔然攻破。

e.note: Juqu Wuhui seized Gaochang in 442 and styled himself King of Liang; the city was taken by the Rouran in 460.

items.note: 460 年柔然立阚伯周为高昌王，此后张、马、麴氏相继为王；麴氏高昌以汉文化为主，立太学。

e.note: In 460 the Rouran made Kan Bozhou King of Gaochang, after whom the Zhang, Ma and Qu clans ruled in turn; the Qu kingdom of Gaochang was predominantly Chinese in culture and set up an Imperial Academy.

items.note: 398 年慕容德自邺南迁滑台称燕王，次年失守。

e.note: In 398 Murong De moved south from Ye to Huatai and styled himself King of Yan; he lost it the following year.

items.note: 曹嶷所筑城，南燕都城；410 年二月被刘裕攻破，城被夷平。

e.note: A city built by Cao Ni and the capital of the Southern Yan; taken by Liu Yu in the 2nd month of 410 and razed.

items.note: 400 年李暠被推为凉公，据敦煌。

e.note: In 400 Li Gao was acclaimed Duke of Liang and held Dunhuang.

items.note: 405 年李暠迁都酒泉，以图东进。

e.note: In 405 Li Gao moved his capital to Jiuquan, planning to advance east.

items.note: 413 年赫连勃勃以叱干阿利督工，蒸土筑城，锥入一寸即杀筑者，城坚可砺刀斧，名统万；遗址今称白城子。

e.note: In 413 Helian Bobo set Chigan Ali to oversee its building; the walls were made of steamed earth, and if an awl could be driven an inch into them the builders were put to death; the walls were hard enough to whet knives and axes on. It was named Tongwan; its ruins are today called Baichengzi.

items.note: 428 年赫连昌被擒后，其弟赫连定在平凉即位。

e.note: After Helian Chang was captured in 428, his younger brother Helian Ding took the throne at Pingliang.

items.note: 丁零翟辽 388 年据滑台称魏天王。

e.note: Zhai Liao of the Dingling occupied Huatai in 388 and styled himself Heavenly King of Wei.

items.note: 405 年谯纵据成都称成都王，413 年七月城破。

e.note: Qiao Zong occupied Chengdu in 405 and styled himself King of Chengdu; the city fell in the 7th month of 413.

items.note: 段龛 350 年据广固称齐王，356 年十一月被前燕攻破。

e.note: Duan Kan occupied Guanggu in 350 and styled himself King of Qi; it was taken by the Former Yan in the 11th month of 356.

items.note: 仇池山“方百顷，四面斗绝”，山上有泉，杨氏据为根据地。

e.note: Mount Chouchi is "a hundred qing in area, sheer on all four sides", with springs on the summit; the Yang clan made it their base.

items.note: 杨氏武兴国都城，506 年被北魏攻灭。

e.note: Capital of the Yang clan's kingdom of Wuxing, destroyed by the Northern Wei in 506.

items.mod: 内蒙古和林格尔土城子
items.note: 386 年拓跋珪复国后以盛乐为都。

e.note: After restoring the state in 386, Tuoba Gui made Shengle his capital.

items.note: 398 年道武帝迁都平城，营建宫室、宗庙、社稷；城西武州山开凿云冈石窟。

e.note: Emperor Daowu moved the capital to Pingcheng in 398 and built palaces, an ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain; the Yungang Grottoes were cut in the Wuzhou Mountains west of the city.

items.mod: 河南洛阳东（汉魏洛阳故城）
items.note: 494 年孝文帝迁都洛阳，在西晋旧址上重建，外郭东西二十里、南北十五里，有佛寺一千三百余所（《洛阳伽蓝记》）。

e.mod: east of Luoyang, Henan (Han–Wei Luoyang city site)
e.note: Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang in 494 and rebuilt it on the old Western Jin site; the outer walls ran twenty li east to west and fifteen li north to south, and the city had more than 1,300 Buddhist temples (Record of the Buddhist Monasteries of Luoyang).

items.note: 534 年高欢迁孝静帝于邺，在旧城南增筑邺南城。

e.note: In 534 Gao Huan moved Emperor Xiaojing to Ye and built the Southern City of Ye south of the old city.

items.note: 北齐都城，以晋阳为别都；577 年正月被北周攻破。

e.note: Capital of Northern Qi, with Jinyang as a secondary capital; taken by the Northern Zhou in the 1st month of 577.

items.note: 高欢的大丞相府所在，号称霸府；东魏政令多出于此。

e.note: Seat of Gao Huan's Grand Chancellor's office, known as the "hegemon's headquarters"; most Eastern Wei orders issued from here.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 534 年孝武帝西奔长安，次年宇文泰立文帝，西魏都长安。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
e.note: In 534 Emperor Xiaowu fled west to Chang'an; the following year Yuwen Tai enthroned Emperor Wen, and the Western Wei had its capital at Chang'an.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 北周都城，581 年二月静帝禅位于杨坚。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city site)
e.note: Capital of the Northern Zhou; in the 2nd month of 581 Emperor Jing abdicated in favor of Yang Jian.

items.note: 隋初暂居汉长安旧城，582 年命宇文恺于其东南营建新都，583 年三月迁入，名大兴城；宫城、皇城、外郭城三重，外郭一百零八坊，为当时世界最大的城市。

e.note: The early Sui court stayed for a time in the old Han city of Chang'an; in 582 Yuwen Kai was ordered to build a new capital to its southeast, which the court moved into in the 3rd month of 583 and named Daxing City. It had three walled layers (palace city, imperial city and outer city), with 108 wards in the outer city, and was the largest city in the world at the time.

items.note: 悉补野部发祥地，雅砻河谷的青瓦达孜宫为早期赞普驻地。

e.note: Homeland of the Pugyal; the Chingwa Taktse Palace in the Yarlung Valley was the seat of the early tsenpos.

items.note: 羊同（象雄）都城，644 年前后为吐蕃所灭。

e.note: Capital of Yangtong (Zhangzhung), which was destroyed by the Tibetan Empire around 644.

items.note: 柔然可汗的王庭，夏季常在鄂尔浑河、土拉河一带，冬季南移。

e.note: The royal court of the Rouran Qaghan, usually on the Orkhon and Tuul in summer, moving south in winter.

items.note: 突厥可汗牙帐所在的圣山（于都斤、郁督军山），突厥碑铭称“于都斤山林”。

e.note: The sacred mountain where the Turkic Qaghan had his royal camp (Yudujin, Yudujun Mountain); Turkic inscriptions call it "the Ötüken forest".

items.note: 吐谷浑都城，在青海湖西十五里，方形土城，今遗址犹存。

e.note: Capital of the Tuyuhun, 15 li west of Qinghai Lake: a square town with earthen walls, whose ruins survive today.

items.note: 高句丽前期都城，平地有国内城，山上有丸都山城。342 年被前燕攻破，414 年长寿王在城东立好太王碑。

e.note: Early capital of Goguryeo, with Gungnae Fortress on the plain and the mountain fortress of Hwando above. It was sacked by the Former Yan in 342; in 414 King Jangsu set up the Gwanggaeto Stele east of the city.

items.note: 427 年长寿王迁都平壤，大城山城与安鹤宫一带为王城；552 年起在其南修筑长安城。

e.note: King Jangsu moved the capital to Pyongyang in 427, the royal city lying around the Daeseongsan mountain fortress and the Anhak Palace; from 552 the Jangan Fortress was built to the south.

items.note: 高句丽 586 年迁入新筑的长安城（平壤城），隋唐屡次远征的最终目标。668 年九月被李勣、薛仁贵与新罗军攻破。

e.note: In 586 Goguryeo moved into the newly built Jangan Fortress (Pyongyang), the ultimate target of the repeated Sui and Tang expeditions. It was stormed in the 9th month of 668 by Li Ji, Xue Rengui and Silla troops.

items.mod: 韩国首尔（风纳土城一带）
items.note: 百济前期都城，475 年九月被高句丽攻破，盖卤王被杀。

e.note: Early capital of Baekje, taken by Goguryeo in the 9th month of 475, when King Gaero was killed.

items.note: 475 年文周王南迁熊津，武宁王陵在此。

e.note: King Munju moved south to Ungjin in 475; the tomb of King Muryeong is here.

items.note: 百济 538 年迁都泗沘。

e.note: Baekje moved its capital to Sabi in 538.

items.note: 新罗王京，今庆州，又称徐罗伐。

e.note: The royal capital of Silla, today's Gyeongju, also called Seorabeol.

items.note: 倭王权的中心，3 世纪以来的巨大古坟集中于此；6 世纪末推古天皇以飞鸟为都。

e.note: The center of the Wa royal power, where the great mounded tombs of the 3rd century onward are concentrated; at the end of the 6th century Empress Suiko made Asuka her capital.

items.note: 推古天皇以来的倭国政治中心；645 年大化改新后一度迁难波，667 年迁近江大津。

e.note: The political center of Wa from the reign of Empress Suiko on. After the Taika Reform of 645 the court moved for a time to Naniwa, and in 667 to Ōmi-Ōtsu.

items.note: 林邑都城，梵名僧伽补罗（狮子城），在区粟城以南。

e.note: Capital of Linyi, called Simhapura (Lion City) in Sanskrit, south of Qusu City.

items.note: 扶南都城，《梁书》称其“国王居重阁，以木栅为城”。

e.note: Capital of Funan; the Book of Liang says "the king lives in a many-storied building, and the city wall is a wooden stockade".

items.note: 萨珊冬都，库思老一世所建的宫殿大拱门（塔克·基斯拉）至今犹存。

e.note: Winter capital of the Sasanians; the great arch of the palace built by Khosrow I (the Taq-i Kisra) still stands.

items.note: 戴克里先四帝共治时期罗马东部的首府。

e.note: Capital of the Roman East under Diocletian's Tetrarchy.

items.note: 330 年君士坦丁大帝迁都拜占庭，改名君士坦丁堡；查士丁尼 537 年建成圣索菲亚大教堂。

e.note: In 330 Constantine the Great moved the capital to Byzantium and renamed it Constantinople; Justinian completed the Hagia Sophia in 537.

items.note: 摩揭陀古都，笈多王朝都城；法显记其“城中王宫殿皆使鬼神作，累石起墙阙”。

e.note: The ancient capital of Magadha and capital of the Gupta dynasty; Faxian wrote that "the royal palaces in the city were all built by spirits, who piled up stones for walls and gate towers".

items.mod: 斯里兰卡阿努拉德普勒
items.note: 狮子国王都，法显 410—411 年居于城中无畏山寺。

e.note: Royal capital of Simhala; Faxian lived in the city's Abhayagiri monastery in 410–411.

items.cmd: 王濬、杜预、王浑 vs 孙皓、张悌
items.note: 279 年冬晋六路伐吴；280 年二月王濬烧断横江铁锁，三月吴丞相张悌在版桥战死，王濬楼船直抵石头城，孙皓面缚出降。

e.note: In the winter of 279 Jin attacked Wu along six routes; in the 2nd month of 280 Wang Jun burned through the iron chains across the Yangtze, in the 3rd month the Wu Chancellor Zhang Ti was killed in battle at Banqiao, and Wang Jun's towered warships reached Shitou City; Sun Hao came out with his hands bound and surrendered.
e.cmd: Wang Jun (王濬), Du Yu and Wang Hun vs. Sun Hao and Zhang Ti

items.cmd: 齐万年 vs 周处
items.note: 周处奉命以五千人攻齐万年七万之众，主帅司马肜按兵不救，周处力战终日，弓尽矢绝而死。

e.note: Zhou Chu was ordered to attack Qi Wannian's seventy thousand with five thousand men; the commander-in-chief Sima Tong held back his troops and sent no help, and Zhou Chu fought all day until his bows and arrows were spent, and died.

items.cmd: 孟观 vs 齐万年
items.note: 孟观率宿卫兵与关中士卒大小十数战，于中亭大破氐羌，生擒齐万年，关中平定。

e.note: Meng Guan, leading palace guards and Guanzhong troops, fought a dozen battles large and small, crushed the Di and Qiang at Zhongting and captured Qi Wannian alive, and Guanzhong was pacified.

items.sides: 成都王颖 胜 赵王伦
items.cmd: 司马颖 vs 孙会、士猗
items.note: 成都王颖先在黄桥失利，旋即在湨水大破伦军，渡河直趋洛阳，赵王伦败亡。

e.note: After a setback at Huangqiao, Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, soon crushed Sima Lun's army at the Ju River and crossed the Yellow River straight for Luoyang; Sima Lun was defeated and died.
e.sides: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, defeated Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao
e.cmd: Sima Ying vs. Sun Hui and Shi Yi

items.sides: 长沙王乂 胜 成都王颖
items.cmd: 司马乂 vs 陆机
items.note: 陆机率二十余万大军进攻洛阳，在建春门外七里涧大败，死者如积，涧水为之不流；陆机随后被司马颖所杀，临刑叹“华亭鹤唳，岂可复闻乎”。

e.note: Lu Ji attacked Luoyang with more than two hundred thousand men and was routed at Qilijian outside the Jianchun Gate; the dead lay in heaps and the stream stopped flowing. Lu Ji was afterwards killed by Sima Ying, sighing before his execution, "Shall I never again hear the cranes cry at Huating?"
e.sides: Sima Ai, Prince of Changsha, defeated Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu

items.cmd: 罗尚 vs 李特
items.note: 李特攻入成都少城后放松戒备，罗尚夜袭斩李特，流民转由李流、李雄统领。

e.note: After breaking into the Lesser City of Chengdu, Li Te relaxed his guard; Luo Shang attacked by night and beheaded him, and the refugees passed under the command of Li Liu and Li Xiong.

items.cmd: 陶侃 vs 张昌
items.note: 荆州刺史刘弘以陶侃为大都护，在竟陵大破张昌，斩首数万，张昌余部石冰东走扬州。

e.note: Liu Hong, Inspector of Jing Province, made Tao Kan Grand Protector-General; Tao Kan crushed Zhang Chang at Jingling, taking tens of thousands of heads, and Zhang Chang's remaining forces under Shi Bing fled east to Yang Province.

items.sides: 成都王颖 胜 东海王越
items.cmd: 司马颖（石超） vs 司马越
items.note: 司马越奉惠帝北征，在荡阴被石超击溃，惠帝面中三箭，侍中嵇绍以身蔽帝，血溅帝衣而死，惠帝被俘入邺。

e.note: Sima Yue took Emperor Hui north on campaign and was routed by Shi Chao at Dangyin; the emperor was struck in the face by three arrows, the Palace Attendant Ji Shao shielded him with his body and died, his blood splashing the emperor's robes, and Emperor Hui was carried captive into Ye.
e.sides: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, defeated Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai
e.cmd: Sima Ying (Shi Chao) vs. Sima Yue

items.cmd: 石勒 vs 王衍、司马范
items.note: 东海王越死后，十余万晋军护灵柩东归，石勒以轻骑追及，围而射之，“相践如山，无一人得免”，王衍等被杀，晋室主力覆没。

e.note: After the death of Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, more than a hundred thousand Jin troops escorted his coffin east; Shi Le overtook them with light cavalry, surrounded them and shot them down — "they trampled one another into heaps like hills, and not one man escaped". Wang Yan and others were killed, and the main Jin army was annihilated.
e.cmd: Shi Le vs. Wang Yan (王衍) and Sima Fan

items.cmd: 刘曜、王弥、石勒 vs 晋怀帝
items.note: 汉军攻入洛阳，焚烧宫庙，杀王公士民三万余人，掘陵墓，怀帝被俘送平阳。

e.note: The Han army broke into Luoyang, burned the palaces and ancestral temples, killed more than thirty thousand princes, officials and townspeople and dug up the imperial tombs; Emperor Huai was captured and sent to Pingyang.
e.cmd: Liu Yao, Wang Mi and Shi Le vs. Emperor Huai of Jin

items.cmd: 刘曜 vs 晋愍帝、麴允
items.note: 刘曜围长安数月，城中斗米值金二两，人相食；十一月愍帝乘羊车、肉袒衔璧出降，西晋亡。

e.note: Liu Yao besieged Chang'an for months; inside the city a peck of grain cost two taels of gold and people ate one another. In the 11th month Emperor Min rode out in a goat cart, stripped to the waist with a jade disc in his mouth, and surrendered, and the Western Jin came to an end.
e.cmd: Liu Yao vs. Emperor Min of Jin and Qu Yun

items.cmd: 石勒 vs 王浚
items.note: 石勒诈称奉戴王浚为帝，以牛羊为贡入蓟城，纵兵大掠，擒王浚送襄国斩首。

e.note: Pretending that he wished to make Wang Jun emperor, Shi Le entered Ji City with oxen and sheep as tribute, let his troops plunder at will, and captured Wang Jun, sending him to Xiangguo to be beheaded.

items.cmd: 祖逖 vs 桃豹
items.note: 祖逖与后赵桃豹分据浚仪城东西台相持四十日，祖逖以布囊盛土诈称米粮，又截获赵军粮车，桃豹宵遁。

e.note: Zu Ti and Tao Bao of the Later Zhao held the eastern and western terraces of Junyi City and faced each other for forty days; Zu Ti filled cloth sacks with earth and passed them off as grain, then captured the Zhao supply carts, and Tao Bao slipped away by night.

items.cmd: 王敦 vs 刘隗、刁协
items.note: 王敦自武昌东下，守石头城的周札开门迎降，官军诸路皆败，刘隗北奔后赵，刁协被杀。

e.note: Wang Dun came down the Yangtze from Wuchang; Zhou Zha, holding Shitou City, opened the gates and surrendered, the government armies were beaten on every front, Liu Wei fled north to the Later Zhao, and Diao Xie was killed.
e.cmd: Wang Dun vs. Liu Wei and Diao Xie

items.cmd: 晋明帝 vs 王含、钱凤
items.note: 王敦再反，命兄王含率五万水陆并进；明帝募壮士夜渡秦淮袭越城，大破王含，王敦闻败病死。

e.note: When Wang Dun rebelled again he sent his elder brother Wang Han forward by land and water with fifty thousand men; Emperor Ming recruited bold men who crossed the Qinhuai by night and attacked Yuecheng, crushing Wang Han, and Wang Dun, hearing of the defeat, died of illness.
e.cmd: Emperor Ming of Jin vs. Wang Han and Qian Feng

items.cmd: 刘曜 vs 石虎
items.note: 石虎率四万攻前赵河东，刘曜亲率精锐救援，在高候大破石虎，乘胜围攻洛阳金墉城。

e.note: Shi Hu attacked the Former Zhao's Hedong with forty thousand men; Liu Yao came to its rescue in person with his best troops, crushed Shi Hu at Gaohou, and followed up by besieging Jinyong City at Luoyang.

items.cmd: 石勒 vs 刘曜
items.note: 石勒亲率步骑四万自大堨渡河，刘曜临阵饮酒数斗，坠马被擒，前赵随即崩溃。

e.note: Shi Le crossed the Yellow River at Da'e at the head of forty thousand foot and horse; Liu Yao drank several pecks of wine before the battle, fell from his horse and was captured, and the Former Zhao promptly collapsed.

items.cmd: 陶侃、温峤 vs 苏峻
items.note: 苏峻乘醉率数骑突阵，坠马被晋军刺杀。

e.note: Su Jun, drunk, charged the enemy line with a few horsemen, fell from his horse and was speared to death by Jin soldiers.
e.cmd: Tao Kan and Wen Jiao vs. Su Jun

items.cmd: 石虎 vs 刘胤、刘熙
items.note: 刘胤率众反攻长安，被石虎大破于义渠，石虎追至上邽，斩刘熙、刘胤以下王公将校三千余人，前赵亡。

e.note: Liu Yin led a counterattack on Chang'an and was crushed by Shi Hu at Yiqu; Shi Hu pursued him to Shanggui and beheaded Liu Xi, Liu Yin and more than three thousand princes, ministers and officers, and the Former Zhao fell.
e.cmd: Shi Hu vs. Liu Yin and Liu Xi

items.cmd: 慕容恪 vs 石虎
items.note: 后赵数十万大军围攻大棘城十余日不下，慕容恪率二千骑追击退兵，斩获三万余级。

e.note: A Later Zhao army several hundred thousand strong besieged Daji City for more than ten days without taking it; Murong Ke pursued the retreating army with two thousand horsemen and took more than thirty thousand heads.

items.sides: 前燕 胜 高句丽
items.cmd: 慕容皝 vs 故国原王
items.note: 慕容皝以主力四万出南道奇袭，攻破丸都，掘美川王墓，掳王母、王妃及男女五万余口而还，高句丽遣使称臣。

e.note: Murong Huang led his main force of forty thousand along the southern road in a surprise attack, sacked Hwando, dug up the tomb of King Micheon, and returned with the king's mother, his queen and more than fifty thousand men and women as captives; Goguryeo sent envoys to declare itself a subject.

items.cmd: 桓温 vs 李势
items.note: 晋军前锋失利，参军龚护战死，箭及桓温马首；鼓吏误击进鼓，袁乔督众力战，大破汉军，李势出降。

e.note: The Jin vanguard faltered, the Adjutant Gong Hu was killed, and arrows reached the head of Huan Wen's horse; but a drummer mistakenly beat the advance, Yuan Qiao urged the men on to fight hard, and they crushed the Han army; Li Shi surrendered.

items.cmd: 谢艾 vs 麻秋
items.note: 前凉谢艾乘轺车、戴白帢，鸣鼓而行，大破后赵麻秋。

e.note: Xie Ai of the Former Liang, riding in a light carriage and wearing a white cap, advanced to the beat of drums and crushed Ma Qiu of the Later Zhao.

items.cmd: 范文 vs 夏侯览
items.note: 林邑王范文攻陷日南郡，杀太守夏侯览及士民五六千人，以日南北界横山为界。

e.note: Fan Wen, King of Linyi, took Rinan Commandery, killed its Administrator Xiahou Lan and five or six thousand of its people, and made the Hengshan range on Rinan's northern edge the border.

items.cmd: 慕容恪 vs 冉闵
items.note: 冉闵连胜十战，慕容恪以铁锁连马为方阵围之，冉闵突围坠马被擒，送龙城斩首。

e.note: Ran Min won ten battles in a row; Murong Ke surrounded him with a square formation of horses linked by iron chains, and Ran Min, breaking out, fell from his horse and was captured, and was sent to Longcheng to be beheaded.

items.cmd: 姚襄 vs 殷浩
items.note: 殷浩北伐，前锋姚襄倒戈伏击，晋军死伤万余，殷浩被废为庶人。

e.note: On Yin Hao's northern expedition, his vanguard under Yao Xiang turned and ambushed him; the Jin army lost more than ten thousand killed and wounded, and Yin Hao was reduced to a commoner.

items.cmd: 桓温 vs 苻苌、苻生
items.note: 桓温自武关入关中，在蓝田大破苻苌，进至灞上，关中父老持牛酒迎于道。

e.note: Huan Wen entered Guanzhong by the Wu Pass, crushed Fu Chang at Lantian and advanced to Bashang, and the elders of Guanzhong met him on the road with oxen and wine.
e.cmd: Huan Wen vs. Fu Chang and Fu Sheng

items.cmd: 苻雄 vs 桓温
items.note: 苻健坚壁清野，苻雄在白鹿原击败桓温，晋军死者万余，桓温粮尽撤退。

e.note: Fu Jian (苻健) cleared the countryside and held his walls; Fu Xiong defeated Huan Wen at Bailuyuan, the Jin army lost more than ten thousand dead, and Huan Wen, out of grain, withdrew.

items.cmd: 桓温 vs 姚襄
items.note: 桓温亲披甲督战，大破姚襄于伊水北岸，收复洛阳。

e.note: Huan Wen put on his armor and directed the battle himself, crushed Yao Xiang on the north bank of the Yi River, and recovered Luoyang.

items.cmd: 苻黄眉、邓羌 vs 姚襄
items.note: 姚襄进图关中，邓羌诱其出战，斩姚襄，其弟姚苌率众降秦。

e.note: Yao Xiang moved to take Guanzhong; Deng Qiang lured him out to fight and killed him, and his younger brother Yao Chang led their followers in surrender to Qin.
e.cmd: Fu Huangmei and Deng Qiang vs. Yao Xiang

items.cmd: 慕容恪 vs 段龛
items.note: 慕容恪围广固数月，筑室反耕，城中人相食，段龛出降。

e.note: Murong Ke besieged Guanggu for months, building houses and turning to farming; inside the city people ate one another, and Duan Kan surrendered.

items.cmd: 慕容恪、慕容垂 vs 沈劲
items.note: 前燕围洛阳一年，守将沈劲以五百人坚守，城破被俘，不屈而死。

e.note: The Former Yan besieged Luoyang for a year; its commander Shen Jin held out with five hundred men, was captured when the city fell, and died unbowed.
e.cmd: Murong Ke and Murong Chui vs. Shen Jin

items.cmd: 慕容垂、慕容德 vs 桓温
items.note: 桓温舟师进至枋头，燕军截断粮道，桓温焚舟陆退，在襄邑遭伏，死者三万余人。

e.note: Huan Wen's fleet reached Fangtou; the Yan army cut his supply line, and Huan Wen burned his boats and withdrew overland, was ambushed at Xiangyi, and lost more than thirty thousand dead.
e.cmd: Murong Chui and Murong De vs. Huan Wen

items.cmd: 王猛 vs 慕容评
items.note: 慕容评拥兵三十万，卖泉鬻薪以谋私利；王猛以六万之众夜袭，大破燕军，斩俘十五万。

e.note: Murong Ping, commanding three hundred thousand men, sold spring water and firewood for his own profit; Wang Meng made a night attack with sixty thousand men, crushed the Yan army, and killed or captured a hundred and fifty thousand.

items.cmd: 苻丕 vs 朱序
items.note: 苻丕率十七万众围城近一年，朱序之母韩氏率婢女增筑西北角城墙，后人称“夫人城”；督护李伯护开门降秦。

e.note: Fu Pi besieged the city for nearly a year with 170,000 men; Zhu Xu's mother, Lady Han, led her maids in building up the northwest corner of the walls, which later generations called the "Lady's Wall"; the Area Protector Li Bohu opened the gates and surrendered to Qin.

items.cmd: 谢玄 vs 俱难、彭超
items.note: 谢玄率北府兵在三阿、盱眙、淮阴连破秦军，最后在君川大胜，俱难、彭超北逃。

e.note: Xie Xuan with the Northern Headquarters Army defeated the Qin army again and again at San'e, Xuyi and Huaiyin, and finally won a great victory at Junchuan; Ju Nan and Peng Chao fled north.
e.cmd: Xie Xuan vs. Ju Nan and Peng Chao

items.cmd: 刘牢之 vs 梁成
items.note: 刘牢之以精兵五千夜渡洛涧，斩秦将梁成等十将，秦军死者万五千人。

e.note: Liu Laozhi crossed the Luojian by night with five thousand picked troops and beheaded the Qin general Liang Cheng and nine other commanders; the Qin army lost fifteen thousand dead.

items.cmd: 谢石、谢玄、谢琰、桓伊 vs 苻坚、苻融
items.note: 晋军八万请秦军稍退以便渡水决战，秦军一退不可止，朱序在阵后大呼“秦军败矣”，苻融坠马被杀，秦军溃散，“风声鹤唳，草木皆兵”。

e.note: The eighty-thousand-strong Jin army asked the Qin army to draw back a little so that it could cross the river and fight a decisive battle; once the Qin army began to retreat it could not be stopped. Zhu Xu shouted from behind its lines, "The Qin army is beaten!", Fu Rong fell from his horse and was killed, and the Qin army broke up — "every gust of wind and cry of a crane, every bush and tree, seemed an enemy soldier".
e.cmd: Xie Shi, Xie Xuan, Xie Yan and Huan Yi vs. Fu Jian and Fu Rong

items.cmd: 吕光 vs 白纯
items.note: 吕光西征围龟兹，龟兹王白纯请狯胡等七十余万骑来援，吕光结阵大破之，西域三十余国降服；鸠摩罗什随之东归。

e.note: On his western expedition Lü Guang besieged Kucha; Bai Chun, King of Kucha, called in more than seven hundred thousand horsemen of the Kuaihu and others to his aid, but Lü Guang drew up his army and crushed them, and more than thirty states of the Western Regions submitted; Kumarajiva went back east with him.

items.cmd: 慕容垂 vs 慕容永
items.note: 慕容垂分兵三路，自滏口入天井关，慕容永集兵台壁，被后燕击溃，长子城破，西燕亡。

e.note: Murong Chui divided his army into three columns and entered by the Tianjing Pass from Fukou; Murong Yong massed his troops at Taibi and was routed by the Later Yan, Zhangzi fell, and the Western Yan came to an end.

items.cmd: 姚兴 vs 苻登
items.note: 苻登被姚兴截断水源，大败于废桥，被擒杀，前秦实亡。

e.note: Cut off from water by Yao Xing, Fu Deng was routed at Feiqiao, captured and killed; the Former Qin was finished in all but name.

items.cmd: 拓跋珪 vs 慕容宝
items.note: 燕军撤退途中在参合陂扎营，魏军夜行追及，日出后乘高俯冲，燕军四五万人放仗请降，被拓跋珪尽数坑杀。

e.note: On its retreat the Yan army camped at Canhe Slope; the Wei army marched through the night to catch up and, at sunrise, charged down from the heights. Forty or fifty thousand Yan soldiers laid down their arms and begged to surrender, and Tuoba Gui had them all buried alive.

items.cmd: 拓跋珪 vs 慕容宝
items.note: 慕容宝夜袭柏肆魏营，魏军初乱，拓跋珪重整击退燕军，燕军大溃，慕容宝随即弃中山北逃。

e.note: Murong Bao made a night attack on the Wei camp at Baisi; the Wei army was thrown into confusion at first, but Tuoba Gui regrouped and drove the Yan army off, the Yan army broke, and Murong Bao soon abandoned Zhongshan and fled north.

items.cmd: 拓跋珪 vs 姚平、姚兴
items.note: 姚平被围柴壁，姚兴率四万援军隔汾水不能救，姚平投水而死，后秦自此不敢东犯。

e.note: Yao Ping was besieged at Chaibi; Yao Xing, with forty thousand relief troops on the other side of the Fen River, could not save him, and Yao Ping threw himself into the water and died. From then on the Later Qin never dared to strike east.
e.cmd: Tuoba Gui vs. Yao Ping and Yao Xing

items.cmd: 刘裕 vs 孙恩
items.note: 孙恩率众十余万、楼船千余艘溯江而上进攻京口，刘裕以数百人在蒜山力战破之。

e.note: Sun En sailed up the Yangtze with more than a hundred thousand followers and over a thousand towered ships to attack Jingkou; Liu Yu with a few hundred men fought hard at Mount Suan and defeated him.

items.cmd: 刘裕 vs 桓谦、卞范之
items.note: 刘裕自京口进军，因风纵火，桓玄军大溃，桓玄挟安帝西逃。

e.note: Liu Yu advanced from Jingkou and set fires with the wind behind him; Huan Xuan's army broke, and Huan Xuan fled west, taking Emperor An with him.
e.cmd: Liu Yu vs. Huan Qian and Bian Fanzhi

items.cmd: 刘毅、何无忌 vs 桓玄
items.note: 桓玄舟师二万被刘毅以火攻击破，逃回江陵，旋即被杀。

e.mod: in the Yangtze at Ezhou, Hubei
e.note: Huan Xuan's twenty-thousand-strong fleet was broken by Liu Yi with fire; Huan Xuan fled back to Jiangling and was soon killed.
e.cmd: Liu Yi and He Wuji vs. Huan Xuan

items.cmd: 刘裕 vs 慕容超
items.note: 晋军以车四千乘为两翼方阵推进，檀韶乘虚袭取临朐城，燕军大溃，慕容超逃回广固。

e.note: The Jin army advanced in a square formation flanked by four thousand carts; Tan Shao seized the city of Linqu while it was left unguarded, the Yan army broke, and Murong Chao fled back to Guanggu.

items.cmd: 刘裕 vs 慕容超
items.note: 晋军围广固八个月，四面攻城，城破，慕容超被俘斩于建康，城被夷平。

e.note: The Jin army besieged Guanggu for eight months and attacked from all four sides; the city fell, Murong Chao was captured and beheaded at Jiankang, and the city was razed.

items.cmd: 卢循、徐道覆 vs 刘毅
items.note: 卢循以八艚舰顺流而下，大破刘毅舟师，进逼建康。

e.note: Lu Xun came down the Yangtze with his eight-hold warships, crushed Liu Yi's fleet, and pressed on toward Jiankang.
e.cmd: Lu Xun and Xu Daofu vs. Liu Yi

items.cmd: 刘裕 vs 卢循
items.note: 刘裕在左里以火攻焚卢循舟舰，卢循南逃广州。

e.note: At Zuoli Liu Yu burned Lu Xun's ships with fire, and Lu Xun fled south to Guang Province.

items.cmd: 刘裕（丁旿、朱超石） vs 长孙嵩
items.note: 刘裕以车百乘列阵于黄河北岸，两端抱河，形如新月，魏骑三万冲阵，晋军以大弩、长槊击之，魏军死伤遍野。

e.note: Liu Yu drew up a hundred carts on the north bank of the Yellow River, both ends resting on the river, in the shape of a crescent moon; thirty thousand Wei horsemen charged the line, and the Jin troops struck them with great crossbows and long lances, leaving the field covered with Wei dead and wounded.
e.cmd: Liu Yu (Ding Wu and Zhu Chaoshi) vs. Zhangsun Song

items.cmd: 王镇恶 vs 姚泓
items.note: 王镇恶率水军沿渭水而上，至渭桥令士卒登岸，舟船任其漂去，背水而战，大破秦军，姚泓出降。

e.note: Wang Zhen'e led his fleet up the Wei River; at the Wei Bridge he ordered his men ashore and let the boats drift away, fought with the river at his back, crushed the Qin army, and Yao Hong surrendered.

items.cmd: 赫连璝 vs 刘义真
items.note: 刘义真弃长安东撤，军中满载宝货、妇女，日行十里，在青泥被夏军追及大败，仅以身免。

e.note: Liu Yizhen abandoned Chang'an and withdrew east, his army so laden with treasure and women that it covered only ten li a day; overtaken by the Xia army at Qingni, it was routed, and he barely escaped with his life.

items.cmd: 奚斤、拓跋嗣 vs 毛德祖
items.note: 毛德祖坚守二百余日，魏军挖地道断其水源，城破被俘，宋失河南。

e.note: Mao Dezu held out for more than two hundred days; the Wei army dug tunnels to cut off his water, and when the city fell he was captured, and Song lost Henan.
e.cmd: Xi Jin and Tuoba Si vs. Mao Dezu

items.cmd: 拓跋焘 vs 赫连昌
items.note: 太武帝以轻骑三万奔袭，佯退诱夏军出城，遇风雨逆击大破之，攻入统万城。

e.note: Emperor Taiwu raced to Tongwan with thirty thousand light horsemen, feigned a retreat to lure the Xia army out of the city, turned on it in a storm of wind and rain, crushed it, and broke into Tongwan City.

items.cmd: 安颉 vs 朱修之
items.note: 到彦之北伐后，朱修之孤守滑台数月，粮尽城陷；檀道济来援，“唱筹量沙”全军而还。

e.note: After Dao Yanzhi's northern expedition, Zhu Xiuzhi held Huatai alone for months until his grain ran out and the city fell; Tan Daoji, coming to the rescue, brought his whole army home by "counting sand as if it were grain".

items.mod: 甘肃临夏一带黄河渡口
items.cmd: 慕璝 vs 赫连定
items.note: 赫连定率十余万众西渡黄河欲袭北凉，吐谷浑以三万骑乘其半渡截击，生擒赫连定，夏亡。

e.mod: a Yellow River ford around Linxia, Gansu
e.note: Helian Ding led more than a hundred thousand people west across the Yellow River intending to attack the Northern Liang; the Tuyuhun struck with thirty thousand horsemen while they were halfway across and captured Helian Ding alive, and Xia came to an end.

items.cmd: 拓跋焘 vs 沮渠牧犍
items.note: 太武帝亲征，围姑臧一月，沮渠牧犍出降，北魏统一北方。

e.note: Emperor Taiwu campaigned in person and besieged Guzang for a month; Juqu Mujian surrendered, and the Northern Wei unified the north.

items.cmd: 陈宪 vs 拓跋焘
items.note: 太武帝以十万骑围悬瓠，筑高楼临城俯射，守将陈宪以不满千人坚守四十二日，魏军死者万余，撤围北归。

e.note: Emperor Taiwu surrounded Xuanhu with a hundred thousand horsemen and built tall towers to shoot down into the city; its commander Chen Xian held out for forty-two days with fewer than a thousand men, and the Wei army, having lost more than ten thousand dead, raised the siege and went back north.

items.cmd: 拓跋焘 vs 王玄谟
items.note: 王玄谟围滑台不下，太武帝渡河来救，号称百万，鞞鼓之声震动天地，王玄谟大败南逃。

e.note: Wang Xuanmo besieged Huatai without taking it; Emperor Taiwu crossed the river to relieve it with an army said to number a million, its drums shaking heaven and earth, and Wang Xuanmo was routed and fled south.

items.cmd: 臧质、沈璞 vs 拓跋焘
items.note: 魏军自瓜步北还途中围攻盱眙三十日，以钩车拉城，城中以铁锁拒之，魏军死者万计，焚掠而归。

e.note: On its way back north from Guabu the Wei army besieged Xuyi for thirty days, pulling at the walls with hook carts while the defenders held them off with iron chains; having lost tens of thousands dead, it burned and plundered as it went home.
e.cmd: Zang Zhi and Shen Pu vs. Tuoba Tao

items.cmd: 尉元 vs 张永、沈攸之
items.note: 宋军欲夺回彭城，天寒雪大，冻死者大半，被尉元截断粮道大败，淮北从此不守。

e.note: The Song army set out to retake Pengcheng; in bitter cold and heavy snow more than half its men froze to death, and when Yu Yuan cut its supply line it was routed; from then on the land north of the Huai could not be held.
e.cmd: Yu Yuan vs. Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi

items.cmd: 慕容白曜 vs 沈文秀
items.note: 慕容白曜围东阳三年，469 年正月城破，沈文秀被俘，青州入魏。

e.note: Murong Baiyao besieged Dongyang for three years; in the 1st month of 469 the city fell, Shen Wenxiu was captured, and Qing Province passed to Wei.

items.sides: 高句丽 胜 百济
items.cmd: 长寿王 vs 盖卤王
items.note: 长寿王率兵三万围攻汉城，七日攻破北城，盖卤王出逃被俘杀，百济南迁熊津。

e.note: King Jangsu besieged Hanseong with thirty thousand men and took the northern city in seven days; King Gaero fled and was captured and killed, and Baekje moved south to Ungjin.

items.cmd: 柳世隆 vs 沈攸之
items.note: 沈攸之率十万大军顺流东下，围郢城三十余日不下，部众逃散，自缢而死。

e.note: Shen Youzhi came down the Yangtze with an army of a hundred thousand and besieged Yingcheng for more than thirty days without taking it; his followers deserted, and he hanged himself.

items.cmd: 元英、孝文帝 vs 崔慧景、萧衍
items.note: 魏军攻克宛城、新野后，孝文帝在邓城大破齐军，萧衍等退保樊城。

e.note: After the Wei army had taken Wancheng and Xinye, Emperor Xiaowen crushed the Qi army at Dengcheng, and Xiao Yan and others fell back to hold Fancheng.
e.cmd: Yuan Ying and Emperor Xiaowen vs. Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan

items.sides: 萧衍 胜 东昏侯
items.cmd: 萧衍 vs 萧宝卷
items.note: 萧衍顺流而下，在新亭、朱雀航连破齐军，围建康台城；十二月东昏侯被卫尉张稷等所杀。

e.note: Xiao Yan came down the Yangtze, defeated the Qi army again and again at Xinting and the Zhuque Pontoon, and besieged Taicheng in Jiankang; in the 12th month the Marquis of Donghun was killed by the Commandant of the Guards Zhang Ji and others.
e.sides: Xiao Yan defeated the Marquis of Donghun

items.cmd: 元英 vs 蔡道恭
items.note: 元英围义阳百余日，守将蔡道恭病死，城中粮尽出降，义阳三关入魏。

e.note: Yuan Ying besieged Yiyang for more than a hundred days; its commander Cai Daogong died of illness, the city ran out of grain and surrendered, and the Three Passes of Yiyang passed to Wei.

items.cmd: 韦叡、曹景宗 vs 元英、杨大眼
items.note: 魏军数十万围钟离，在邵阳洲两岸架设浮桥；韦叡、曹景宗乘淮水暴涨以火船焚桥，魏军溺死十余万、被斩亦如之，五万人被俘。

e.note: A Wei army several hundred thousand strong besieged Zhongli, building pontoon bridges from both banks to Shaoyang Islet; Wei Rui and Cao Jingzong, taking advantage of a sudden rise of the Huai, burned the bridges with fire ships; more than a hundred thousand Wei soldiers drowned, as many were cut down, and fifty thousand were captured.
e.cmd: Wei Rui and Cao Jingzong vs. Yuan Ying and Yang Dayan

items.sides: 破六韩拔陵 胜 北魏
items.cmd: 破六韩拔陵 vs 李崇、元渊
items.note: 北魏派李崇北讨，在五原被破六韩拔陵大败，六镇局势失控。

e.note: The Northern Wei sent Li Chong north to put down the rising, but he was routed by Poliuhan Baling at Wuyuan, and the situation in the Six Garrisons slipped out of control.
e.cmd: Poliuhan Baling vs. Li Chong and Yuan Yuan

items.sides: 尔朱荣 胜 葛荣
items.cmd: 尔朱荣 vs 葛荣
items.note: 葛荣号称百万，尔朱荣以七千精骑隐蔽山谷，以三人为伍，持棒不持刀，突入敌阵，生擒葛荣。

e.note: Ge Rong was said to command a million men; Erzhu Rong hid seven thousand picked horsemen in the mountain valleys, formed them in groups of three armed with clubs rather than swords, charged into the enemy ranks, and captured Ge Rong alive.

items.cmd: 陈庆之 vs 杨昱、元天穆
items.note: 陈庆之以七千白袍军攻荥阳，北魏三十万援军将至，陈庆之激励将士登城，一举攻克，又击败元天穆的援军。

e.note: Chen Qingzhi attacked Xingyang with his seven thousand white-robed troops; with three hundred thousand Northern Wei relief troops about to arrive, he roused his men to scale the walls, took the city in a single assault, and then defeated Yuan Tianmu's relief army.
e.cmd: Chen Qingzhi vs. Yang Yu and Yuan Tianmu

items.cmd: 尔朱荣 vs 元颢、陈庆之
items.note: 尔朱荣在硖石夜渡黄河，大破元颢之子元冠受，元颢弃洛阳南逃被杀，陈庆之的军队溃散。

e.note: Erzhu Rong crossed the Yellow River by night at Xiashi and crushed Yuan Guanshou, son of Yuan Hao; Yuan Hao abandoned Luoyang, fled south and was killed, and Chen Qingzhi's army broke up.
e.cmd: Erzhu Rong vs. Yuan Hao and Chen Qingzhi

items.sides: 尔朱天光 胜 万俟丑奴
items.cmd: 尔朱天光、贺拔岳 vs 万俟丑奴
items.note: 尔朱天光扬言天热暂停，乘万俟丑奴分兵屯田之际突袭，生擒万俟丑奴，关陇平定。

e.note: Erzhu Tianguang announced that he would pause for the hot weather, then struck suddenly while Moqi Chounu had split his forces to farm, captured him alive, and pacified Guanlong.
e.cmd: Erzhu Tianguang and Heba Yue vs. Moqi Chounu

items.sides: 高欢 胜 尔朱兆
items.cmd: 高欢 vs 尔朱兆
items.note: 高欢用离间计使尔朱兆与尔朱仲远等互相猜疑，在广阿大败尔朱兆，俘获五千余人。

e.note: Gao Huan used stratagems to sow mutual suspicion between Erzhu Zhao and Erzhu Zhongyuan and the rest, routed Erzhu Zhao at Guang'e, and took more than five thousand prisoners.

items.sides: 高欢 胜 尔朱氏
items.cmd: 高欢 vs 尔朱兆、尔朱天光、尔朱度律、尔朱仲远
items.note: 高欢以步兵不足三万、骑兵二千，连牛驴塞断归路，布圆阵死战，大破尔朱氏二十万之众。

e.note: With fewer than thirty thousand foot and two thousand horse, Gao Huan blocked his own line of retreat with tethered oxen and donkeys, drew up in a circular formation, fought to the death, and crushed the Erzhu host of two hundred thousand.
e.cmd: Gao Huan vs. Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Tianguang, Erzhu Dulü and Erzhu Zhongyuan

items.cmd: 宇文泰 vs 窦泰
items.note: 高欢三路西攻，宇文泰佯退长安，实以六千骑奔袭小关，窦泰全军覆没，自杀。

e.note: Gao Huan attacked west along three routes; Yuwen Tai pretended to fall back on Chang'an but actually raced to Xiaoguan with six thousand horsemen; Dou Tai's whole army was wiped out and he killed himself.

items.cmd: 宇文泰 vs 高欢
items.note: 宇文泰以不足万人背水东西列阵，伏兵于苇中，东魏二十万人争进乱阵，伏兵四起，东魏丧甲士八万，弃铠仗十八万。
