e.note: With fewer than ten thousand men Yuwen Tai drew up east to west with the river at his back and hid troops in the reeds; the two hundred thousand Eastern Wei troops jostled forward in disorder, the ambush sprang from all sides, and the Eastern Wei lost eighty thousand armored men and abandoned 180,000 suits of armor and weapons.

items.cmd: 侯景、高敖曹 vs 宇文泰、独孤信
items.note: 两军在河桥、邙山一带大战，雾起不辨敌我，东魏高敖曹战死，西魏李虎、独孤信等先退，宇文泰烧营西归。

e.note: The two armies fought a great battle around Heqiao and Mount Mang; fog rose so that friend could not be told from foe. Gao Aocao of the Eastern Wei was killed, but Li Hu, Dugu Xin and others of the Western Wei withdrew first, and Yuwen Tai burned his camp and went back west.
e.cmd: Hou Jing and Gao Aocao vs. Yuwen Tai and Dugu Xin

items.cmd: 高欢 vs 宇文泰
items.note: 首日西魏大胜，几乎擒获高欢；次日东魏反攻，西魏大败，宇文泰仅以身免，死伤六万余人。

e.note: On the first day the Western Wei won a great victory and nearly captured Gao Huan; the next day the Eastern Wei counterattacked and routed the Western Wei, Yuwen Tai barely escaping with his life, with more than sixty thousand killed and wounded.

items.cmd: 韦孝宽 vs 高欢
items.note: 高欢昼夜攻城五十余日，挖地道、造攻车、断汾水，韦孝宽皆随机应对，东魏死者七万，高欢忧愤成疾，次年病死。

e.note: Gao Huan attacked the city day and night for more than fifty days — digging tunnels, building siege engines and cutting off the Fen River — and Wei Xiaokuan met every move; the Eastern Wei lost seventy thousand dead, and Gao Huan fell ill from grief and anger and died the following year.

items.cmd: 慕容绍宗 vs 萧渊明
items.note: 梁军筑寒山堰壅泗水灌彭城，慕容绍宗率十万来援，大破梁军，俘主帅萧渊明。

e.note: The Liang army built the Hanshan Dam on the Si to flood Pengcheng; Murong Shaozong came to its rescue with a hundred thousand men, crushed the Liang army, and captured its commander Xiao Yuanming.

items.cmd: 慕容绍宗 vs 侯景
items.note: 侯景与慕容绍宗相持数月，粮尽，部众溃散，率八百骑南逃寿阳。

e.note: Hou Jing faced Murong Shaozong for several months until his grain ran out and his followers deserted, and he fled south to Shouyang with eight hundred horsemen.

items.cmd: 侯景 vs 梁武帝、羊侃
items.note: 侯景围台城一百三十余日，筑土山、引玄武湖水灌城，城中饿死者大半；三月城破，梁武帝被软禁饿死。

e.note: Hou Jing besieged Taicheng for more than 130 days, building earthen mounds and turning the waters of Xuanwu Lake on the city, and more than half of those inside starved to death; in the 3rd month the city fell, and Emperor Wu of Liang was held under house arrest and starved to death.
e.cmd: Hou Jing vs. Emperor Wu of Liang and Yang Kan

items.cmd: 王僧辩 vs 侯景
items.note: 侯景率军西上攻巴陵，王僧辩偃旗息鼓坚守，侯景昼夜攻城不下，军中疫病，退还建康。

e.note: Hou Jing led his army west to attack Baling; Wang Sengbian furled his banners, silenced his drums and held firm, and Hou Jing, unable to take the city by attacking day and night and with sickness spreading in his army, fell back to Jiankang.

items.cmd: 王僧辩、陈霸先 vs 侯景
items.note: 梁军在石头城北立栅，陈霸先分兵奋击，侯景大败东逃，四月在海上被部下所杀。

e.note: The Liang army built a stockade north of Shitou City, and Chen Baxian struck hard with separate columns; Hou Jing was routed and fled east, and in the 4th month he was killed at sea by his own men.
e.cmd: Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian vs. Hou Jing

items.cmd: 陆法和、樊猛 vs 萧纪
items.note: 萧纪率军东下，陆法和在峡口立铁锁拒之，后路被西魏切断，萧纪兵败被杀。

e.mod: mouth of the Xiling Gorge, Yichang, Hubei
e.note: Xiao Ji led his army down the Yangtze; Lu Fahe stretched iron chains across the gorge mouth to stop him, and with his rear cut off by the Western Wei, Xiao Ji was defeated and killed.
e.cmd: Lu Fahe and Fan Meng vs. Xiao Ji

items.sides: 西魏 胜 萧纪余部
items.cmd: 尉迟迥 vs 萧撝
items.note: 尉迟迥经剑阁南下，围成都五十日，萧撝出降，巴蜀入西魏。

e.note: Yuchi Jiong came south by way of Jiange and besieged Chengdu for fifty days; Xiao Hui surrendered, and Ba-Shu passed to the Western Wei.
e.sides: Western Wei defeated Xiao Ji's remaining forces

items.cmd: 于谨、杨忠、宇文护 vs 梁元帝
items.note: 西魏五万大军攻破江陵，梁元帝焚古今图书十四万卷出降，被杀，江陵官民男女数万口被掳北迁。

e.note: A Western Wei army of fifty thousand took Jiangling; Emperor Yuan of Liang burned 140,000 scrolls of books old and new and surrendered, and was killed, and tens of thousands of the officials and townspeople of Jiangling, men and women, were carried off north.
e.cmd: Yu Jin, Yang Zhong and Yuwen Hu vs. Emperor Yuan of Liang

items.cmd: 金武力 vs 百济圣王
items.note: 百济圣王为报新罗夺取汉江下游之仇，联合大伽倻进攻管山城，圣王被新罗伏兵所杀，百济大败。

e.note: To avenge Silla's seizure of the lower Han River, King Seong of Baekje joined Daegaya in attacking Gwansanseong; he was killed by a Silla ambush, and Baekje was routed.
e.cmd: Kim Mu-ryeok vs. King Seong of Baekje

items.sides: 陈霸先 胜 北齐
items.cmd: 陈霸先 vs 萧轨
items.note: 北齐十万大军渡江进逼建康，陈霸先在钟山、覆舟山北冒雨决战，大破齐军，斩北齐将领四十六人。

e.note: A Northern Qi army of a hundred thousand crossed the Yangtze and pressed on Jiankang; Chen Baxian fought a decisive battle in the rain north of Mount Zhong and Mount Fuzhou, crushed the Qi army, and beheaded forty-six Northern Qi commanders.

items.cmd: 侯瑱 vs 王琳
items.note: 王琳与北齐军顺流东下，侯瑱乘西南风反攻，以拍竿击沉王琳战舰，王琳投奔北齐。

e.note: Wang Lin came down the Yangtze with the Northern Qi army; Hou Tian counterattacked with a southwest wind behind him and sank Wang Lin's warships with striking booms, and Wang Lin fled to Northern Qi.

items.sides: 北齐 胜 北周·突厥
items.cmd: 段韶、斛律光 vs 杨忠、木杆可汗
items.note: 北周与突厥联军冒雪攻晋阳，北齐以精兵出城迎战，突厥不战而退，周军大败。

e.note: The combined Northern Zhou and Turkic armies attacked Jinyang through the snow; Northern Qi sent its best troops out of the city to meet them, the Turks withdrew without fighting, and the Zhou army was routed.
e.sides: Northern Qi defeated Northern Zhou and the Turks
e.cmd: Duan Shao and Hulü Guang vs. Yang Zhong and Muqan Qaghan

items.cmd: 兰陵王高长恭、段韶、斛律光 vs 宇文护（尉迟迥）
items.note: 北周二十万大军围洛阳三十日，兰陵王以五百骑冲入周军重围，至金墉城下，城上弓弩齐发，周军溃退；齐人作《兰陵王入阵曲》。

e.note: A Northern Zhou army of two hundred thousand besieged Luoyang for thirty days; the Prince of Lanling charged through the Zhou encirclement with five hundred horsemen to the foot of Jinyong City, the crossbows on the walls loosed together, and the Zhou army broke and withdrew; the people of Qi composed the song "The Prince of Lanling Enters the Fray".
e.cmd: Gao Changgong (Prince of Lanling), Duan Shao and Hulü Guang vs. Yuwen Hu (Yuchi Jiong)

items.sides: 陈 胜 华皎·北周
items.cmd: 吴明彻、淳于量 vs 华皎、宇文直
items.note: 湘州刺史华皎叛陈，北周、后梁出兵相助；陈军乘风发拍竿击毁敌船，大破之，华皎奔江陵。

e.note: Hua Jiao, Inspector of Xiang Province, rebelled against Chen with troops from the Northern Zhou and Later Liang; the Chen army, with the wind behind it, smashed the enemy ships with striking booms and crushed them, and Hua Jiao fled to Jiangling.
e.sides: Chen defeated Hua Jiao and Northern Zhou
e.cmd: Wu Mingche and Chunyu Liang vs. Hua Jiao and Yuwen Zhi

items.cmd: 吴明彻 vs 王琳、皮景和
items.note: 吴明彻堰肥水灌寿阳，城中多病，十月攻破，斩王琳，北齐援军数十万望风而退。

e.note: Wu Mingche dammed the Fei River to flood Shouyang, and sickness spread in the city; in the 10th month he took it and beheaded Wang Lin, and the Northern Qi relief army of several hundred thousand withdrew at the first sight of him.
e.cmd: Wu Mingche vs. Wang Lin and Pi Jinghe

items.cmd: 宇文邕 vs 高纬
items.note: 北周攻克平阳，齐后主率大军反攻围城，周武帝亲至城下决战，齐后主与冯淑妃并骑观战先逃，齐军大溃。

e.note: After the Northern Zhou took Pingyang, the Last Ruler of Qi counterattacked with a great army and besieged the city; Emperor Wu of Zhou came to the walls in person to fight a decisive battle, the Last Ruler, watching the battle on horseback beside Consort Feng, fled first, and the Qi army broke.

items.cmd: 宇文邕 vs 高恒
items.note: 周军进围邺城，齐后主禅位于八岁太子后东逃，城破，北齐亡。

e.note: The Zhou army advanced to besiege Ye; the Last Ruler of Qi abdicated in favor of his eight-year-old crown prince and fled east, the city fell, and Northern Qi came to an end.

items.cmd: 王轨 vs 吴明彻
items.note: 吴明彻堰泗水围彭城，北周王轨率军在清水入淮处以铁锁连车轮沉于水中，截断归路，陈军三万全军覆没，吴明彻被俘。

e.note: Wu Mingche dammed the Si to besiege Pengcheng; Wang Gui of the Northern Zhou sank cart wheels joined by iron chains in the water where the Qing River enters the Huai, cutting off the line of retreat, and the Chen army of thirty thousand was wiped out and Wu Mingche captured.

items.sides: 杨坚 胜 尉迟迥
items.cmd: 韦孝宽 vs 尉迟迥
items.note: 尉迟迥以十余万众列阵邺城南，观战百姓数万，韦孝宽先射观战者，迥军大乱，城破，尉迟迥自杀。

e.note: Yuchi Jiong drew up more than a hundred thousand men south of Ye, with tens of thousands of townspeople watching; Wei Xiaokuan first shot at the onlookers, Yuchi Jiong's army fell into confusion, the city fell, and Yuchi Jiong killed himself.

items.cmd: 弗里提根 vs 罗马皇帝瓦伦斯
items.note: 被匈人逼入罗马境内的哥特人起而反抗，在阿德里安堡歼灭罗马主力，皇帝瓦伦斯战死。

e.note: The Goths, driven into Roman territory by the Huns, rose in revolt and annihilated the main Roman army at Adrianople; the emperor Valens was killed in battle.
e.cmd: Fritigern vs. the Roman emperor Valens

items.cmd: 沙普尔二世 vs 罗马皇帝尤利安
items.note: 尤利安率大军深入美索不达米亚，在泰西封城下取胜却无法攻城，撤退途中中矛而死，继位的约维安割让尼西比斯等地求和。

e.note: Julian led a great army deep into Mesopotamia and won a battle beneath the walls of Ctesiphon but could not take the city; on the retreat he was struck by a spear and died, and his successor Jovian ceded Nisibis and other places to make peace.
e.cmd: Shapur II vs. the Roman emperor Julian

items.cmd: 嚈哒王 vs 卑路斯
items.note: 萨珊王卑路斯第三次进攻嚈哒，陷入预先挖好的壕沟，全军覆没，卑路斯战死，萨珊此后向嚈哒纳贡。

e.note: On his third attack on the Hephthalites the Sasanian king Peroz fell into a trench dug in advance; his whole army was destroyed and he was killed, and thereafter the Sasanians paid tribute to the Hephthalites.

items.cmd: 贝利萨留 vs 菲鲁兹
items.note: 东罗马名将贝利萨留在达拉城前掘壕布阵，击败兵力倍于己的萨珊军。

e.note: The great Eastern Roman general Belisarius dug trenches and drew up his army before the city of Dara, and defeated a Sasanian army twice the size of his own.

items.sides: 天竺诸王 胜 嚈哒
items.cmd: 耶输达曼 vs 摩醯逻矩罗
items.note: 摩腊婆王耶输达曼联合诸王击败嚈哒王摩醯逻矩罗，嚈哒势力退出恒河流域。

e.note: Yashodharman, King of Malwa, allied with other kings, defeated the Hephthalite king Mihirakula, and Hephthalite power withdrew from the Ganges valley.

items.cmd: 土门 vs 阿那瓌
items.note: 突厥土门可汗大破柔然于怀荒北，阿那瓌自杀，柔然汗国瓦解。

e.note: Tumen Qaghan of the Turks crushed the Rouran north of Huaihuang; Anagui killed himself, and the Rouran Qaghanate collapsed.

items.mod: 乌兹别克斯坦卡尔希一带
items.sides: 突厥·波斯 胜 嚈哒
items.cmd: 室点密、库思老一世 vs 嚈哒王
items.note: 突厥西部室点密可汗与萨珊库思老一世南北夹击，嚈哒在那色波（卡尔希）一带战败，国亡，乌浒水以北归突厥，以南归萨珊。

e.note: Istämi Qaghan of the western Turks and Khosrow I of the Sasanians attacked from north and south; the Hephthalites were defeated around Nasaf (Qarshi) and their state was destroyed, the land north of the Oxus passing to the Turks and that south of it to the Sasanians.
e.sides: The Turks and Persia defeated the Hephthalites
e.cmd: Istämi and Khosrow I vs. Hephthalite king

items.note: 灭吴之后晋武帝颁行占田、课田之制与户调式，规定男女占田与课田的限额，并按品级荫客、荫亲属。

e.note: After the conquest of Wu, Emperor Wu of Jin issued the zhantian and ketian land statutes and the household tax schedule, fixing limits on the land that men and women might hold and on which they would be taxed, and allowing officials, by rank, to shelter dependents and relatives from taxation.

items.note: 武帝以诸子分镇关中、荆州、扬江等要地，掌握兵权，为八王之乱埋下伏笔。

e.note: Emperor Wu posted his sons to key regions — Guanzhong, Jing Province, and Yang and Jiang Provinces — with command of troops, sowing the seeds of the War of the Eight Princes.

items.note: 贾后借楚王玮诛杨骏、杀汝南王亮，再诛楚王玮，八王之乱由此开端。

e.note: Empress Jia used Sima Wei, Prince of Chu, to execute Yang Jun and kill Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, then executed Sima Wei — the beginning of the War of the Eight Princes.

items.note: 赵王伦与孙秀矫诏废杀贾后，次年篡位，三王起兵讨伐。

e.old: Coup of Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao
e.note: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Sun Xiu forged an edict, deposed and killed Empress Jia, and usurped the throne the following year, when three princes rose against him.

items.note: 匈奴左贤王刘渊在左国城称汉王，以“兴汉”为号召，十六国由此开端。

e.old: Liu Yuan proclaims himself King of Han
e.note: Liu Yuan, Worthy King of the Left of the Xiongnu, proclaimed himself King of Han at Zuoguo City under the banner of "reviving Han" — the beginning of the Sixteen Kingdoms.

items.note: 六郡流民首领李雄在成都称成都王，306 年称帝，国号大成。

e.old: Li Xiong proclaims himself King of Chengdu
e.note: Li Xiong, leader of the refugees of six commanderies, proclaimed himself King of Chengdu at Chengdu, and in 306 emperor, naming his state Great Cheng.

items.note: 琅邪王司马睿以安东将军镇建邺，王导为其谋主，南渡士族与江东豪族由此结合。

e.note: Sima Rui, Prince of Langya, took up his post at Jianye as General Who Pacifies the East, with Wang Dao as his chief adviser; from this the émigré northern clans and the great families of Jiangdong came together.

items.note: 永嘉之乱后中原士民大批南迁江左，史称“衣冠南渡”；东晋在江南侨置北方州郡安置流民。

e.note: After the Disaster of Yongjia the gentry and people of the Central Plain moved south of the Yangtze in great numbers — "the flight of the caps and gowns to the south"; the Eastern Jin set up émigré northern provinces and commanderies in the south to settle the refugees.

items.note: 祖逖率部曲百余家渡江北伐，中流击楫而誓“不能清中原而复济者，有如大江”。

e.mod: on the Yangtze around Zhenjiang, Jiangsu
e.note: Zu Ti crossed the Yangtze on a northern expedition with over a hundred households of his retainers, striking his oar in midstream and swearing: "If I cannot clear the Central Plain and cross back, may I be like this great river!"

items.note: 高句丽美川王攻灭乐浪郡，次年取带方郡，汉魏晋在朝鲜半岛的郡县统治告终。

e.note: King Micheon of Goguryeo destroyed Lelang Commandery and took Daifang Commandery the following year, ending the commandery rule of the Han, Wei and Jin on the Korean peninsula.

items.note: 318 年三月司马睿即皇帝位（元帝），“王与马，共天下”。

e.note: In the 3rd month of 318 Sima Rui ascended the imperial throne (Emperor Yuan) — "the Wang and the Ma share the realm".

items.note: 靳准在平阳杀汉主刘粲，尽诛刘氏男女，掘刘渊、刘聪陵墓，自称汉天王。

e.note: Jin Zhun killed the Han ruler Liu Can at Pingyang, put every man and woman of the Liu clan to death, dug up the tombs of Liu Yuan and Liu Cong, and styled himself Heavenly King of Han.

items.note: 石勒在襄国即皇帝位，立太学、小学，命州郡察举，又设“君子营”网罗士人。

e.note: Shi Le took the imperial throne at Xiangguo, set up an Imperial Academy and lesser schools, ordered the provinces and commanderies to recommend men for office, and formed a "Gentlemen's Camp" to gather in scholars.

items.mod: 山西浑源一带（繁畤之北）
items.note: 拓跋什翼犍在繁畤之北即代王位，设置百官，制定法律，建元建国；340 年迁都盛乐。

e.note: North of Fanzhi, Tuoba Shiyijian became King of Dai, set up a bureaucracy, drew up laws and proclaimed the era name Jianguo; in 340 he moved his capital to Shengle.

items.note: 慕容皝在柳城之北筑龙城，构宫殿宗庙，342 年迁都。

e.note: Murong Huang built Longcheng north of Liucheng, with palaces and an ancestral temple, and moved his capital there in 342.

items.note: 慕容皝亲征宇文部，宇文逸豆归远走漠北而死，宇文部五千余落被迁徙昌黎。

e.note: Murong Huang campaigned in person against the Yuwen; Yuwen Yidougui fled far north of the Gobi and died, and more than five thousand Yuwen tents were moved to Changli.

items.note: 冉闵下令“赵人斩一胡首送凤阳门者，文官进位三等，武职悉拜牙门”，邺城内外死者二十余万。

e.note: Ran Min ordered that "any man of Zhao who brings the head of a Hu to the Fengyang Gate will be promoted three ranks if a civil official, and made a Gate General if a military officer"; more than two hundred thousand died in and around Ye.

items.note: 三月三日王羲之与谢安、孙绰等四十一人在会稽山阴兰亭修禊，曲水流觞，王羲之作《兰亭集序》。

e.note: On the third day of the third month Wang Xizhi, Xie An, Sun Chuo and others, forty-one men in all, held the spring purification at the Orchid Pavilion in Shanyin, Kuaiji, floating wine cups down a winding stream, and Wang Xizhi wrote the Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Poems.

items.note: 沙门乐僔在鸣沙山东麓开凿第一个洞窟，此后历代续凿，即敦煌莫高窟。

e.mod: eastern foot of Mingsha Mountain, Dunhuang, Gansu
e.note: The monk Le Zun cut the first cave at the eastern foot of Mingsha Mountain; later generations went on cutting more — the Mogao Caves of Dunhuang.

items.note: 前秦苻坚派僧人顺道送佛像、经文至高句丽，小兽林王立太学、颁律令。

e.note: Fu Jian (苻坚) of the Former Qin sent the monk Sundo to Goguryeo with Buddhist images and scriptures; King Sosurim set up an Imperial Academy and issued laws.

items.note: 谢玄出镇广陵，招募南渡的北方流民中的骁勇之士，组建北府兵，刘牢之、何谦等为将。

e.note: Xie Xuan, taking up his post at Guangling, recruited the boldest of the northern refugees who had fled south and formed the Northern Headquarters Army, with Liu Laozhi, He Qian and others as its commanders.

items.note: 苻坚被姚苌所俘，拒绝交出传国玺、禅位，被缢杀于新平佛寺，时年四十八。

e.note: Fu Jian was captured by Yao Chang; refusing to hand over the imperial seal or abdicate, he was strangled in a Buddhist temple at Xinping, at the age of forty-eight.

items.mod: 内蒙古乌兰察布一带（牛川）
items.note: 拓跋珪在牛川召集旧部，即代王位，四月改称魏王。

e.note: Tuoba Gui gathered the old followers of Dai at Niuchuan and became King of Dai, changing the title to King of Wei in the 4th month.

items.note: 五斗米道首领孙恩自海岛起兵，攻陷会稽，三吴八郡响应，前后持续四年。

e.note: Sun En, a leader of the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice, rose from the offshore islands and took Kuaiji; the eight commanderies of the Three Wu rose in answer, and the rebellion lasted four years in all.

items.note: 后秦姚兴迎龟兹高僧鸠摩罗什至长安，在逍遥园西明阁主持译经，十余年间译出《法华》《维摩》《中论》等经论三百余卷。

e.note: Yao Xing of the Later Qin brought the eminent Kuchean monk Kumarajiva to Chang'an, where he led the translation of scriptures in the Ximing Pavilion of the Xiaoyao Garden, producing in a little over ten years more than three hundred scrolls of sutras and treatises, among them the Lotus, the Vimalakirti and the Middle Treatise.

items.note: 柔然社仑统一漠北，自称丘豆伐可汗，“可汗”之称自此始见于北方。

e.note: Shelun of the Rouran united the lands north of the Gobi and styled himself Qiudoufa Qaghan; this is the first appearance of the title "Qaghan" in the north.

items.note: 刘裕与何无忌、刘毅等二十七人在京口、广陵同时起兵讨伐桓玄。

e.note: Liu Yu, He Wuji, Liu Yi and others, twenty-seven men in all, rose at Jingkou and Guangling at the same time against Huan Xuan.

items.note: 陶渊明为彭泽令八十余日，不为五斗米折腰，赋《归去来兮辞》辞官归隐。

e.old: Tao Yuanming withdraws to the countryside
e.note: Tao Yuanming served as magistrate of Pengze for little more than eighty days; refusing to "bow for five pecks of rice", he resigned his post and withdrew to the countryside, writing "Homeward Bound".

items.note: 赫连勃勃发岭北胡汉十万人筑统万城，蒸土筑墙，“统一天下，君临万邦”。

e.note: Helian Bobo sent a hundred thousand Hu and Chinese from north of the ridges to build Tongwan City with walls of steamed earth, naming it "to unify all under heaven and rule over ten thousand states".

items.note: 高句丽长寿王为其父广开土王立碑，记其南征百济、新罗、击退倭兵等功业。

e.note: King Jangsu of Goguryeo set up a stele to his father King Gwanggaeto recording his deeds, including his campaigns south against Baekje and Silla and his repulse of the Wa.

items.note: 刘裕受晋恭帝禅位，国号宋，东晋亡。

e.note: Liu Yu accepted the abdication of Emperor Gong of Jin and named his dynasty Song; the Eastern Jin came to an end.

items.note: 长寿王自国内城迁都平壤，经营半岛南部。

e.old: Goguryeo moves its capital to Pyongyang
e.note: King Jangsu moved the capital from Gungnae Fortress to Pyongyang and turned to the south of the peninsula.

items.note: 倭王赞、珍、济、兴、武自 421 年至 478 年先后十余次遣使南朝宋，求封“安东大将军、倭国王”及都督诸国军事。

e.old: The Five Kings of Wa send envoys
e.note: The Wa kings San, Chin, Sei, Kō and Bu sent envoys to Liu Song more than ten times between 421 and 478, seeking the titles "Grand General Who Pacifies the East, King of Wa" and command over the armies of several states.

items.note: 太武帝在崔浩、寇谦之影响下崇道抑佛，446 年下诏诛杀沙门、焚毁经像，为“三武一宗”法难之首。

e.note: Under the influence of Cui Hao and Kou Qianzhi, Emperor Taiwu favored Daoism and suppressed Buddhism; in 446 he decreed that monks be killed and scriptures and images destroyed — the first of the persecutions of the "Three Wus and One Zong".

items.note: 崔浩主持编修国史，刻石于郊外，直书拓跋先世之事，被诛灭族，牵连清河崔氏及姻亲范阳卢氏、太原郭氏、河东柳氏。

e.note: Cui Hao directed the compilation of the state history and had it carved on stone outside the city, recording plainly the affairs of the early Tuoba; he was executed and his clan wiped out, and the Cui of Qinghe and their relatives by marriage — the Lu of Fanyang, the Guo of Taiyuan and the Liu of Hedong — were drawn in.

items.note: 文成帝复兴佛法，沙门统昙曜在武州山开凿五窟，造像高达七十尺、六十尺。

e.note: Emperor Wencheng revived Buddhism, and Tanyao, Superintendent of Monks, cut five caves in the Wuzhou Mountains with images seventy and sixty feet tall.

items.note: 祖冲之撰《大明历》，首次在历法中引入岁差；又推算圆周率在 3.1415926 与 3.1415927 之间。

e.note: Zu Chongzhi compiled the Daming Calendar, the first calendar to take account of the precession of the equinoxes; he also calculated π to lie between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927.

items.note: 北魏颁行均田令，计口授露田、桑田，次年立三长制；隋唐均田制皆承此而来。

e.note: The Northern Wei issued the equal-field decree, allotting open fields and mulberry fields by head count, and the following year set up the system of the Three Elders; the equal-field systems of Sui and Tang both derived from it.

items.note: 孝文帝以南伐为名迁都洛阳，此后改胡服、断北语、改汉姓、定门第、与汉族通婚。

e.old: Emperor Xiaowen moves the capital to Luoyang
e.note: Ostensibly marching south, Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang; thereafter Xianbei dress and the northern language were given up, Chinese surnames adopted, family ranks fixed, and intermarriage with Chinese encouraged.

items.note: 迁都后北魏皇室在伊阙开凿石窟，古阳洞、宾阳洞相继完成。

e.note: After the move of the capital the Northern Wei imperial house cut grottoes at Yique, completing the Guyang and Binyang caves in turn.

items.note: 孝文帝为天竺僧跋陀在少室山阴立少林寺。

e.note: Emperor Xiaowen founded the Shaolin Monastery on the north side of Mount Shaoshi for the Indian monk Batuo.

items.mod: 安徽五河与江苏泗洪之间
items.note: 梁武帝采纳魏降人王足之议，役军民二十万在浮山筑堰壅淮水以灌寿阳，堰成长九里，516 年九月淮水暴涨堰溃，沿淮城戍居民十余万口漂入海。

e.mod: between Wuhe, Anhui and Sihong, Jiangsu
e.note: Following the advice of Wang Zu, a defector from Wei, Emperor Wu of Liang put two hundred thousand soldiers and civilians to work building a dam at Fushan to hold back the Huai and flood Shouyang; the finished dam was nine li long. In the 9th month of 516 the Huai rose suddenly and the dam burst, sweeping more than a hundred thousand people of the towns, forts and villages along the river into the sea.

items.note: 沃野镇民破六韩拔陵杀镇将起兵，六镇响应，北魏崩溃由此开始。

e.note: Poliuhan Baling, a garrison soldier of Woye, killed the garrison commander and rose in arms, the Six Garrisons rose in answer, and the collapse of the Northern Wei began.

items.note: 梁武帝四次舍身同泰寺为寺奴，由群臣以巨款赎回；建康佛寺达五百余所，“南朝四百八十寺”。

e.old: Emperor Wu of Liang gives himself to Tongtai Temple
e.note: Emperor Wu of Liang four times gave himself to Tongtai Temple as a temple slave and was redeemed by his ministers for huge sums; the Buddhist temples of Jiankang numbered more than five hundred — "the 480 temples of the Southern Dynasties".

items.note: 尔朱荣在河阴将胡太后与幼主沉入黄河，屠杀王公朝臣二千余人，北魏统治集团元气尽丧。

e.note: At Heyin Erzhu Rong drowned the Empress Dowager Hu and the child emperor in the Yellow River and massacred more than two thousand princes and officials; the Northern Wei ruling elite never recovered.

items.note: 金官伽倻末王金仇亥率王妃、王子降于新罗法兴王，其子金武力即后来的新罗名将金庾信之祖。

e.note: Kim Gu-hae, the last king of Geumgwan Gaya, surrendered to King Beopheung of Silla with his queen and princes; his son Kim Mu-ryeok was the grandfather of the later Silla general Kim Yu-sin.

items.note: 孝武帝西奔宇文泰，高欢另立孝静帝迁都邺城，北魏分裂为东魏、西魏。

e.note: Emperor Xiaowu fled west to Yuwen Tai, Gao Huan set up Emperor Xiaojing and moved the capital to Ye, and the Northern Wei split into the Eastern and Western Wei.

items.note: 百济圣王迁都泗沘，改国号南扶余；同年（一说 552 年）遣使向倭国传入佛像、经论。

e.old: Baekje moves its capital to Sabi
e.note: King Seong of Baekje moved the capital to Sabi and renamed the state Southern Buyeo; in the same year (or 552) he sent envoys to bring Buddhist images and scriptures to Wa.

items.note: 交州豪族李贲 541 年起兵逐梁刺史萧谘，544 年称南越帝，国号万春。

e.note: Lý Bí, of a great family of Jiao Province, rose in 541 and drove out the Liang Inspector Xiao Zi; in 544 he proclaimed himself Emperor of Southern Yue, naming his state Vạn Xuân.

items.note: 侯景以诛朱异为名在寿阳起兵反梁，联络临贺王萧正德为内应。

e.note: Hou Jing rose against Liang at Shouyang, claiming he would execute Zhu Yi, and won over Xiao Zhengde, Prince of Linhe, as his inside man.

items.note: 高洋废东魏孝静帝自立，国号齐。

e.note: Gao Yang deposed Emperor Xiaojing of Eastern Wei and took the throne himself, naming his dynasty Qi.

items.note: 551 年新罗与百济联手攻高句丽，收复汉江流域；553 年新罗背盟夺取百济所得的汉江下游，置新州。

e.old: Silla takes the Han River basin
e.note: In 551 Silla and Baekje joined forces against Goguryeo and recovered the Han River basin; in 553 Silla broke the alliance and seized the lower Han River that Baekje had gained, setting up Sinju.

items.note: 突厥土门可汗大破柔然后自称伊利可汗，以于都斤山为牙帐，突厥汗国建立。

e.note: After crushing the Rouran, Tumen Qaghan of the Turks styled himself Il Qaghan and set up his royal camp at Ötüken: the Turkic Qaghanate was founded.

items.note: 557 年正月宇文觉代西魏称周天王，十月陈霸先代梁建陈。

e.note: In the 1st month of 557 Yuwen Jue replaced the Western Wei and took the title Heavenly King of Zhou, and in the 10th month Chen Baxian replaced Liang and founded Chen.

items.note: 新罗真兴王派异斯夫攻灭大伽倻，伽倻诸国尽入新罗。

e.note: King Jinheung of Silla sent Isabu to destroy Daegaya, and all the Gaya states passed to Silla.

items.old: 突厥使团至君士坦丁堡
items.note: 西突厥室点密可汗派粟特人马尼亚赫出使东罗马，商议绕过萨珊直接贸易丝绸，次年东罗马派蔡马库斯回访突厥牙帐。

e.note: Istämi Qaghan of the Western Turks sent the Sogdian Maniakh as envoy to the Eastern Roman Empire to arrange direct trade in silk bypassing the Sasanians; the following year the Eastern Roman Empire sent Zemarchus to the Turkic royal camp in return.

items.note: 北周武帝下诏禁断佛、道二教，毁经像，令沙门、道士还俗，577 年灭北齐后推行于齐境。

e.old: Emperor Wu of Zhou's persecution of Buddhism
e.note: Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou banned both Buddhism and Daoism, destroyed scriptures and images, and ordered monks and Daoist priests to return to lay life; after conquering Northern Qi in 577 he extended the ban to the former Qi lands.

items.note: 北周静帝禅位于丞相杨坚，隋朝建立，年号开皇。

e.note: Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou abdicated in favor of the Chancellor Yang Jian, and the Sui dynasty was founded with the era name Kaihuang.

items.note: 旃陀罗笈多一世在摩揭陀即位，建立笈多王朝，以华氏城为都。

e.note: Chandragupta I took the throne in Magadha and founded the Gupta dynasty, with its capital at Pataliputra.

items.note: 君士坦丁大帝召集基督教主教会议，制定《尼西亚信经》。

e.note: Constantine the Great convened a council of Christian bishops, which drew up the Nicene Creed.

items.note: 君士坦丁大帝迁都拜占庭，改名君士坦丁堡，号称“新罗马”。

e.note: Constantine the Great moved the capital to Byzantium and renamed it Constantinople, calling it the "New Rome".

items.mod: 俄罗斯伏尔加格勒一带
items.note: 匈人渡过伏尔加河、顿河西进，击破阿兰人与东哥特人，哥特诸部被迫请求进入罗马境内。

e.note: The Huns crossed the Volga and the Don moving west and crushed the Alans and the Ostrogoths; the Gothic tribes were forced to ask to be let into Roman territory.

items.note: 狄奥多西一世死后，帝国由二子分治，东罗马以君士坦丁堡为都。

e.old: Roman Empire divided between East and West
e.note: After the death of Theodosius I the empire was divided between his two sons, the Eastern Roman Empire having its capital at Constantinople.

items.note: 笈多王朝鸠摩罗笈多一世（约 415—455）时始建那烂陀寺，后成为天竺最大的佛教学府。

e.note: Nalanda was founded under Kumaragupta I of the Gupta dynasty (c. 415–455), and later became the greatest center of Buddhist learning in India.

items.note: 约 552 年两名僧侣受查士丁尼之托，把蚕卵藏在空心手杖中从东方带到君士坦丁堡，东罗马从此养蚕织丝。

e.note: Around 552 two monks, commissioned by Justinian, hid silkworm eggs in hollow canes and brought them from the East to Constantinople, and thereafter the Eastern Roman Empire raised silkworms and wove silk.

items.note: 关中东大门，东汉末年设关以代函谷。417 年王镇恶自潼关沿渭水直抵长安，537 年宇文泰自此东出，在小关伏击东魏窦泰。

e.note: The eastern gate of Guanzhong, established at the end of the Eastern Han to replace the Hangu Pass. In 417 Wang Zhen'e went from Tong Pass up the Wei River straight to Chang'an; in 537 Yuwen Tai came out east through it and ambushed Dou Tai of the Eastern Wei at Xiaoguan.

items.note: 黄河蒲坂渡口，连通关中与河东；537 年高欢自此渡河攻西魏，兵败沙苑。

e.note: The Yellow River ford at Puban, linking Guanzhong with Hedong; in 537 Gao Huan crossed here to attack the Western Wei and was defeated at Shayuan.

items.note: 长安东南门户，经上洛通往南阳、襄阳；354 年桓温第一次北伐即由此入关中。

e.note: The southeastern gateway of Chang'an, leading by way of Shangluo to Nanyang and Xiangyang; in 354 Huan Wen entered Guanzhong this way on his first northern expedition.

items.note: 秦岭北口，扼陈仓道入汉中、蜀中，南北朝时为关中与汉中的分界。

e.note: The northern mouth of the Qinling, commanding the Chencang Road into Hanzhong and Shu; under the Northern and Southern Dynasties it marked the boundary between Guanzhong and Hanzhong.

items.note: 翻越陇山的要道，关中与陇右的分界。

e.note: The main road over the Long Mountains, marking the boundary between Guanzhong and Longyou.

items.note: 关中西北门户，扼泾水上游，前秦、后秦、夏、北魏在此反复争夺。

e.note: The northwestern gateway of Guanzhong, commanding the upper Jing; the Former Qin, Later Qin, Xia and Northern Wei fought over it again and again.

items.note: 金牛道上的天险，西晋张载《剑阁铭》称“一人荷戟，万夫趑趄”；553 年尉迟迥由此南下取蜀。

e.note: A natural fortress on the Jinniu Road; the Western Jin writer Zhang Zai, in his Inscription on Jiange, wrote that "one man with a halberd can make ten thousand falter"; in 553 Yuchi Jiong came south this way to take Shu.

items.note: 长江三峡西口，鱼复白帝城在此，扼巴蜀东门。

e.note: The western entrance to the Three Gorges of the Yangtze, where Baidi City at Yufu stood, commanding the eastern gate of Ba-Shu.

items.note: 洛阳东门户，又称成皋，北临黄河、南连嵩山。423 年毛德祖坚守二百余日后陷于北魏，543 年邙山之战因高仲密以虎牢降西魏而起。

e.note: The eastern gate of Luoyang, also called Chenggao, with the Yellow River to the north and Mount Song to the south. In 423 it fell to the Northern Wei after Mao Dezu had held it for more than two hundred days; the Battle of Mount Mang in 543 began when Gao Zhongmi surrendered Hulao to the Western Wei.

items.note: 太行陉上的关隘，连接上党与河内。

e.note: A pass on the Taihang Defile, linking Shangdang and Henei.

items.note: 太行八陉之一，河东与河北间的孔道；396 年拓跋珪分兵东出井陉，进围中山。

e.note: One of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang, the passage between Hedong and Hebei; in 396 Tuoba Gui sent columns east through Jingxing to besiege Zhongshan.

items.note: 太行八陉之一，代北通往中山的孔道。

e.note: One of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang, the passage from northern Dai to Zhongshan.

items.note: 句注山上的关隘，河东北面屏障；310 年拓跋猗卢得句注陉以北五县，此关即为晋与代的分界。

e.note: A pass on Mount Gouzhu, the northern shield of Hedong; in 310 Tuoba Yilu gained the five counties north of the Gouzhu Defile, and the pass became the boundary between Jin and Dai.

items.note: 太行八陉之军都陉，幽州北门。

e.note: The Jundu Defile of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang; the northern gate of You Province.

items.note: 幽州东北通往库莫奚、契丹的要道。

e.note: The main road from You Province northeast to the Kumo Xi and the Khitan.

items.note: 五岭之一，岭南与中原间最重要的通道；410 年卢循、徐道覆北上，分别取道湘江与大庾岭。

e.note: One of the Five Ridges and the most important passage between Lingnan and the Central Plain; in 410 Lu Xun and Xu Daofu marched north by way of the Xiang River and the Dayu Pass respectively.

items.mod: 甘肃敦煌西北（小方盘城）
items.note: 汉代所置，魏晋时仍是出敦煌西行的关口；法显 400 年由敦煌出关，“上无飞鸟，下无走兽”，行十七日至鄯善。

e.note: Set up in Han times, it was still the pass for travelers heading west from Dunhuang under Wei and Jin; Faxian went out through it from Dunhuang in 400 — "no birds in the sky above, no beasts on the ground below" — and reached Shanshan after seventeen days.

items.note: 敦煌西南出西域南道之关。

e.note: The pass southwest of Dunhuang leading to the southern route through the Western Regions.

items.note: 焉耆通往龟兹道上的峡谷关隘，384 年吕光西征即经此攻龟兹。

e.note: A gorge pass on the road from Karasahr to Kucha; Lü Guang went this way to attack Kucha on his western expedition of 384.

items.note: 汉武帝所迁之新关，西晋洛阳西面门户，311 年刘曜自此方向进逼洛阳。

e.note: The new pass to which Emperor Wu of Han moved the old one; the western gate of Western Jin Luoyang, from which direction Liu Yao advanced on Luoyang in 311.

items.note: 自幽州东北出塞通往辽西的古道，慕容、段部与中原往来多经此道。

e.note: The old road going out northeast from You Province beyond the frontier to Liaoxi; most traffic between the Murong, the Duan and the Central Plain went this way.

items.note: 穿越阴山的南北孔道，北魏六镇与盛乐、平城之间的要道。

e.note: The north–south passage through the Yin Mountains, the main road between the Six Garrisons of the Northern Wei and Shengle and Pingcheng.

items.note: 汉中西门，金牛道、陈仓道在此交会，南北朝争夺汉中的必争之地。

e.note: The western gate of Hanzhong, where the Jinniu Road and the Chencang Road met; a point the north and the south had to win in any contest for Hanzhong.

items.mod: 河南信阳南（平靖、武阳、黄岘）
items.note: 大别山西段的平靖、武阳、黄岘三关，扼义阳南下江汉之路；504 年北魏取义阳后三关入魏，此后南北反复争夺。

e.mod: south of Xinyang, Henan (Pingjing, Wuyang and Huangxian)
e.note: The three passes of Pingjing, Wuyang and Huangxian in the western Dabie Mountains, commanding the road south from Yiyang to the Jiang–Han region; after the Northern Wei took Yiyang in 504 the three passes fell to Wei, and thereafter north and south fought over them again and again.

items.note: 巢湖经濡须水入江之口，孙吴以来江淮间的水路要冲。

e.note: The mouth of the Ruxu River, by which Chao Lake drains into the Yangtze; a key point on the waterways between the Yangtze and the Huai since Sun Wu times.

items.note: 长江下游最重要的渡口之一，548 年侯景自此渡江攻建康。

e.note: One of the most important crossings of the lower Yangtze; Hou Jing crossed here to attack Jiankang in 548.

items.mod: 俄罗斯达吉斯坦杰尔宾特
items.note: 里海西岸的关城，萨珊在此筑长墙，扼草原诸族南下之路，东罗马亦曾出资维护。

e.note: A fortress on the west shore of the Caspian where the Sasanians built a long wall to block the steppe peoples' road south; the Eastern Roman Empire also contributed money to its upkeep.

items.note: 关中的南屏，有子午、傥骆、褒斜、陈仓诸谷道入汉中；354 年桓温北伐、553 年尉迟迥取蜀，皆循谷道往来。

e.note: The southern screen of Guanzhong, crossed by the valley roads of Ziwu, Tangluo, Baoye and Chencang into Hanzhong; Huan Wen's northern expedition of 354 and Yuchi Jiong's conquest of Shu in 553 both went by these roads.

items.note: 汉中与巴蜀之间的屏障，米仓道翻越于此。

e.note: The barrier between Hanzhong and Ba-Shu, crossed by the Micang Road.

items.note: 河东与河北的分界，有“太行八陉”沟通；十六国时西燕、后燕、北魏隔此山争并州、河北。

e.note: The boundary between Hedong and Hebei, crossed by the "Eight Defiles of the Taihang"; in the Sixteen Kingdoms period the Western Yan, Later Yan and Northern Wei faced each other across these mountains in contesting Bing Province and Hebei.

items.note: 河东西部山地，西临黄河，刘渊起兵的左国城在其西麓；北朝时为稽胡（山胡）聚居之地。

e.note: The mountains of western Hedong, bordered by the Yellow River on the west; Zuoguo City, where Liu Yuan rose, lay on their western slopes, and under the Northern Dynasties they were home to the Jihu (Mountain Hu).

items.note: 河东之南，盐池在其北麓。

e.note: In southern Hedong; the salt lake lies at their northern foot.

items.note: 北岳，代北与河北之间。

e.note: The Northern Peak, between northern Dai and Hebei.

items.note: 北魏时已有佛寺，北齐时寺院多至二百余所。

e.note: There were already Buddhist temples here under the Northern Wei, and under Northern Qi they numbered more than two hundred.

items.note: 幽州北面屏障，慕容、段部与中原往来的门户。

e.note: The northern shield of You Province and the gateway between the Murong and Duan and the Central Plain.

items.note: 漠南草原与河套之间的屏障；北魏沿其北麓设沃野、怀朔、武川等六镇，防御柔然。

e.note: The barrier between the steppe south of the Gobi and the Hetao; along their northern foot the Northern Wei set up the Six Garrisons — Woye, Huaishuo, Wuchuan and others — against the Rouran.

items.note: 河套西侧屏障，北魏薄骨律镇在其东。

e.note: The western shield of the Hetao, with the Northern Wei Bogulü Garrison to the east.

items.note: 关中与陇右之间的屏障，前秦苻登、后秦姚苌在其东西两侧拉锯多年。

e.note: The barrier between Guanzhong and Longyou, on either side of which Fu Deng of the Former Qin and Yao Chang of the Later Qin fought back and forth for years.

items.note: 河西走廊南侧，河西鲜卑、卢水胡依山游牧。

e.note: On the south side of the Hexi Corridor; the Hexi Xianbei and the Lushui Hu grazed their herds along these mountains.

items.note: 西域南道与青海之间，吐谷浑由此控制鄯善、且末。

e.note: Between the southern route through the Western Regions and Qinghai; from here the Tuyuhun controlled Shanshan and Qiemo.

items.note: 于阗南山，产玉。

e.note: Khotan's southern mountains, a source of jade.

items.note: 黄河绕其而过，吐谷浑的腹地在其北。

e.note: The Yellow River bends around them, and the heartland of the Tuyuhun lay to their north.

items.note: 青藏高原腹地，长江正源发源于此（今名）。

e.note: In the heart of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau; the main source of the Yangtze rises here. The name is modern.

items.note: 藏南谷地北缘（今名）。

e.note: The northern edge of the valleys of southern Tibet. The name is modern.

items.note: 天竺北面的大雪山，法显、宋云西行皆远望其峰。

e.note: The great snowy mountains north of India; Faxian and Song Yun both saw their peaks from afar on their journeys west.

items.note: 西域与中亚的分界，法显 401 年、宋云 519 年先后翻越。

e.note: The divide between the Western Regions and Central Asia, crossed by Faxian in 401 and by Song Yun in 519.

items.note: 北朝称白山，北为柔然、高车、突厥游牧之地，南为焉耆、龟兹等绿洲国家。

e.note: Called the White Mountains under the Northern Dynasties; to the north were the grazing lands of the Rouran, Gaoche and Turks, to the south the oasis states of Karasahr, Kucha and others.

items.note: 阿尔泰山，突厥兴起于金山之阳，为柔然锻铁。

e.note: The Altai, on whose southern side the Turks arose, working iron for the Rouran.

items.note: 杭爱山，漠北腹地，柔然、突厥的牙帐在其东麓。

e.note: The Khangai, in the heart of the land north of the Gobi; the royal camps of the Rouran and the Turks lay at its eastern foot.

items.note: 拓跋鲜卑的发祥地，北魏 443 年遣李敞到嘎仙洞石室祭祖刻辞。

e.note: The homeland of the Tuoba Xianbei; in 443 the Northern Wei sent Li Chang to sacrifice to the ancestors in the stone chamber of the Gaxian Cave and carve an inscription there.

items.note: 长白山，北朝称徒太山，勿吉居其北。

e.note: The Changbai Mountains, called Mount Tutai under the Northern Dynasties; the Wuji lived to their north.

items.note: 辽西名山，前燕龙城在其西。

e.note: A famous mountain of Liaoxi, with the Former Yan capital Longcheng to its west.

items.note: 东岳，南燕、东晋、北魏在其周边反复争夺。

e.note: The Eastern Peak, around which the Southern Yan, the Eastern Jin and the Northern Wei fought again and again.

items.note: 西岳，潼关以西。

e.note: The Western Peak, west of Tong Pass.

items.note: 中岳，495 年北魏孝文帝为天竺僧跋陀建少林寺于其少室山。

e.note: The Central Peak; in 495 Emperor Xiaowen of the Northern Wei founded the Shaolin Monastery for the Indian monk Batuo on Mount Shaoshi, one of its peaks.

items.note: 洛阳与南阳盆地之间。

e.note: Between Luoyang and the Nanyang Basin.

items.note: 淮南与江汉之间，义阳三关在其西段。

e.note: Between Huainan and the Jiang–Han region, with the Three Passes of Yiyang in its western section.

items.note: 长江三峡所在。

e.note: Where the Three Gorges of the Yangtze lie.

items.note: 五溪蛮聚居之地。

e.note: Home of the Five Streams tribes.

items.note: 资水、沅水之间（今名）。

e.note: Between the Zi and Yuan rivers. The name is modern.

items.note: 越城、都庞、萌渚、骑田、大庾五岭，岭南与中原的分界。

e.note: The five ridges of Yuecheng, Dupang, Mengzhu, Qitian and Dayu, forming the divide between Lingnan and the Central Plain.

items.note: 湖南、江西之间（今名）。

e.note: Between Hunan and Jiangxi. The name is modern.

items.note: 闽与江州之间。

e.note: Between Min and Jiang Province.

items.note: 浙、闽之间的山岭。

e.note: Mountains between Zhejiang and Fujian.

items.note: 又称匡庐，东晋慧远在此创东林寺、结白莲社，陶渊明隐居于其南麓。

e.note: Also called Kuanglu; here Huiyuan of the Eastern Jin founded the Donglin Temple and the White Lotus Society, and Tao Yuanming lived in retirement at its southern foot.

items.note: 南岳。

e.note: The Southern Peak.

items.note: 汶山郡所在，羌、邓至诸部居其西北。

e.note: Where Wenshan Commandery lay; the Qiang, the Dengzhi and other tribes lived to its northwest.

items.note: 成都平原西缘，与诸羌相接。

e.note: The western edge of the Chengdu Plain, bordering the Qiang tribes.

items.note: 川西高原东缘（今名）。

e.note: The eastern edge of the western Sichuan plateau. The name is modern.

items.note: 洱海西岸。

e.note: On the west shore of Erhai Lake.

items.note: 南中西南的山脉（今名）。

e.note: A range in the southwest of Nanzhong. The name is modern.

items.note: 吐火罗与天竺之间的屏障；法显、宋云西行皆经其东段，嚈哒与萨珊、天竺争夺山南的罽宾、乾陀罗。

e.note: The barrier between Tokharistan and India; Faxian and Song Yun both crossed its eastern section on their journeys west, and the Hephthalites fought the Sasanians and Indian powers for Jibin and Gandhara south of it.

items.note: 黑海与里海之间的山脉，萨珊与东罗马争夺其南的伊比利亚、亚美尼亚；北方游牧民经杰尔宾特关隘南下。

items.note: 小亚细亚南缘的山脉，东罗马与萨珊边界的西北屏障。

e.note: The mountains along the southern edge of Asia Minor, the northwestern shield of the frontier between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Sasanians.

items.note: 伊朗高原西缘的山脉，萨珊的冬都泰西封在其西麓平原，夏季王庭多在山中。

e.note: The mountains along the western edge of the Iranian Plateau; the Sasanian winter capital Ctesiphon lay on the plain at their western foot, and the royal court often spent the summer in the mountains.

items.note: 伊朗高原北缘、里海南岸的山脉。

e.note: The mountains along the northern edge of the Iranian Plateau, on the south shore of the Caspian.

items.note: 天竺南北的分界，北为中天竺，南为南天竺（德干）。

e.note: The divide between northern and southern India, with Central India to the north and South India (the Deccan) to the south.

items.note: 河东中轴，晋阳、平阳皆临汾水；汉赵、后赵、北齐皆据此与关中对峙。

e.note: The axis of Hedong, on which both Jinyang and Pingyang stood; from here Han Zhao, Later Zhao and Northern Qi each faced Guanzhong.

items.note: 长江上游。

e.note: The upper reaches of the Yangtze.

items.note: 金沙江，225 年诸葛亮“五月渡泸”即此。

e.note: The Jinsha River; Zhuge Liang's "crossing of the Lu in the 5th month" in 225 was here.

items.note: 长江，南北朝的天堑，南北对峙多以江淮为界；450 年北魏太武帝饮马瓜步，548 年侯景自采石渡江。

e.note: The Yangtze, the great natural moat of the Northern and Southern Dynasties; the confrontation of north and south mostly ran along the Yangtze and the Huai. Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei watered his horses at Guabu in 450, and Hou Jing crossed the river at Caishi in 548.

items.note: 辽东与辽西的分界，前燕、后燕、北燕与高句丽长期隔水相争。

e.note: The boundary between Liaodong and Liaoxi, across which the Former Yan, Later Yan and Northern Yan long contended with Goguryeo.

items.note: 沔水，襄阳、樊城夹江而立，南朝雍州重镇，萧衍即由此起兵。

e.note: The Mian River; Xiangyang and Fancheng faced each other across it, forming the great stronghold of Yong Province under the Southern Dynasties; Xiao Yan rose in arms from here.

items.note: 江州豫章临其下游。

e.note: Yuzhang in Jiang Province lay on its lower course.

items.note: 色楞格河，敕勒（高车）诸部游牧之地。

e.note: The Selenga, grazing land of the Chile (Gaoche) tribes.

items.note: 交州龙编临其右岸。

e.note: Longbian in Jiao Province lay on its right bank.

items.note: 蜀地西南的大河，介于成都平原与越巂之间。

e.note: A great river in the southwest of Shu, between the Chengdu Plain and Yuexi.

items.note: 西拉木伦河，契丹、库莫奚游牧于其流域。

e.note: The Xar Moron, in whose valley the Khitan and the Kumo Xi grazed their herds.

items.note: 松花江，夫余、勿吉居其流域。

e.note: The Songhua, in whose valley the Buyeo and the Wuji lived.

items.note: 成都平原的水源，都江堰在其上。

e.note: The water source of the Chengdu Plain, with the Dujiangyan irrigation works on it.

items.note: 南中西部的大河，永昌在其西。

e.note: A great river in the west of Nanzhong, with Yongchang to its west.

items.note: 代北与幽州之间的大河，平城在其支流如浑水畔。

e.note: A great river between northern Dai and You Province; Pingcheng stood on its tributary, the Ruhun River.

items.note: 雅鲁藏布江，悉补野部发祥的雅隆河谷在其南岸。

e.note: The Yarlung Tsangpo; the Yarlung valley, birthplace of the Pugyal, lies on its south bank.

items.note: 唐称涪陵江、黔江。

e.note: Called the Fuling River or the Qian River in Tang times.

items.note: 湘州长沙临湘水。

e.note: Changsha in Xiang Province lay on the Xiang.

items.note: 南北朝长期以淮为界，寿阳、钟离、盱眙、淮阴等沿淮重镇反复易手；514—516 年梁筑浮山堰壅淮，堰溃死者十余万。

e.note: Under the Northern and Southern Dynasties the Huai long marked the border, and the great strongholds along it — Shouyang, Zhongli, Xuyi, Huaiyin — changed hands again and again; in 514–516 Liang built the Fushan Dam across it, and when the dam burst more than a hundred thousand died.

items.note: 建溪、富屯溪汇合后经福州入海。

e.note: Formed where the Jian and Futun streams meet, it flows past Fuzhou into the sea.

items.note: 西汉水，自武兴、晋寿南下巴西。

e.note: The Western Han River, flowing south from Wuxing and Jinshou to Baxi.

items.note: 经韶州南下广州，大庾岭道的水路部分。

e.note: Flowing south past Shaozhou to Guangzhou, the river section of the Dayu Pass route.

items.note: 勿吉诸部居其流域。

e.note: The Wuji tribes lived in its valley.

items.note: 百济前期都城汉城临其下游；475 年高句丽攻陷汉城，551—553 年新罗夺取汉江流域。

e.note: Baekje's early capital, Hanseong, stood on its lower course; Goguryeo took Hanseong in 475, and Silla seized the Han River basin in 551–553.

items.note: 晋南北朝时黄河下游大致沿东汉王景所治河道，经滑台、碻磝北，于千乘入海。滑台、碻磝、虎牢、洛阳号称“河南四镇”，为南北争夺的焦点。今黄河下游（虚线）为 1855 年改道后所走。

e.note: Under the Jin and the Northern and Southern Dynasties the lower Yellow River broadly followed the course regulated by Wang Jing of the Eastern Han, passing north of Huatai and Qiao'ao and entering the sea at Qiansheng. Huatai, Qiao'ao, Hulao and Luoyang were called the "four garrisons south of the river" and were the focus of the struggle between north and south. The modern lower Yellow River (dashed) follows the course taken after the change of 1855.

items.note: 鸭绿江，高句丽故都丸都（国内城）临其中游。

e.note: The Yalu; the old Goguryeo capital Hwando (Gungnae Fortress) lay on its middle course.

items.note: 黑龙江。

e.note: The Amur.

items.note: 蒙兀室韦居其东。

e.note: The Mengwu Shiwei lived to its east.

items.note: 关中命脉，417 年王镇恶率水军沿渭水直抵长安城下。

e.note: The lifeline of Guanzhong; in 417 Wang Zhen'e led his fleet up the Wei River straight to the walls of Chang'an.

items.note: 于阗产玉之河。

e.note: The river of Khotan that yields jade.

items.note: 流经安定、新平入渭，关中西北的门户。

e.note: Flowing past Anding and Xinping into the Wei, the northwestern gateway of Guanzhong.

items.note: 邺城在其南岸，后赵、冉魏、前燕、东魏、北齐相继都此。

e.note: Ye lay on its south bank, capital in turn of the Later Zhao, Ran Wei, Former Yan, Eastern Wei and Northern Qi.

items.note: 鄂尔浑河，柔然、突厥的牙帐皆在其上游一带。

e.note: The Orkhon; the royal camps of both the Rouran and the Turks were around its upper course.

items.mod: 古济水（今黄河下游大部即其故道）
items.note: 济水自巨野泽东北流入海，又称清河；417 年刘裕溯清水入河，以“却月阵”破北魏。

e.mod: old Ji River (the lower Yellow River now runs mostly in its bed)
e.note: The Ji flowed northeast from the Juye Marsh to the sea and was also called the Qing; in 417 Liu Yu went up the Qing into the Yellow River and broke the Northern Wei with his "Crescent Formation".

items.note: 洛阳城南的大河。

e.note: The great river south of Luoyang.

items.note: 流经伊阙，北魏在此开凿龙门石窟；356 年桓温在伊水北岸大破姚襄。

e.note: It flows through Yique, where the Northern Wei cut the Longmen Grottoes; in 356 Huan Wen crushed Yao Xiang on its north bank.

items.note: 流经杏城、冯翊入渭。

e.note: Flows past Xingcheng and Pingyi into the Wei River.

items.note: 悬瓠城在其畔，450 年陈宪守悬瓠四十二日。

e.note: Xuanhu stood on its bank, where Chen Xian held out for forty-two days in 450.

items.note: 南北朝时淮北的要道，颍川、汝阴诸郡依此。

e.note: A main route north of the Huai under the Northern and Southern Dynasties, along which the commanderies of Yingchuan, Ruyin and others lay.

e.note: A waterway between north and south; the northern expeditions of Liu Yu and Wu Mingche both went north along the Si. In 578 Wang Gui cut the Qing River at Lüliang, and the Chen army was wiped out.

items.note: 流经真定（常山）城南，河北中部的大河。

e.note: Flowing past the south of Zhending (Changshan), the great river of central Hebei.

items.note: 南阳盆地主河，于襄州入汉。

items.note: 经灵渠与湘水相通。

items.note: 鄯州临湟水。

e.note: Shanzhou stood on the Huangshui.

items.note: 流经甘州，北入居延海。

items.note: 巴尔喀什湖，悦般、高车先后游牧于其南。

e.note: Lake Balkhash, south of which the Yueban and the Gaoche grazed their herds in turn.

items.note: 贝加尔湖，敕勒诸部居其南。

items.note: 勿吉诸部居其周边。

items.note: 博斯腾湖，焉耆国临其西。

items.note: 黄河源头的湖泊，在吐谷浑南境。

items.note: 濡须水由此入江。

e.note: The Ruxu River carries its waters into the Yangtze.

items.note: 巴陵临其东北，551 年王僧辩在巴陵挫败侯景。

e.note: Baling lay on its northeast shore, where Wang Sengbian thwarted Hou Jing in 551.

items.note: 伊塞克湖。

e.note: Lake Issyk-Kul.

items.note: 吐谷浑的中心，6 世纪夸吕在湖西筑伏俟城为都。

e.note: The center of the Tuyuhun; in the 6th century Kualü built Fuqi City west of the lake as his capital.

items.note: 罗布泊，楼兰（鄯善）故地在其西，魏晋西域长史驻海头。

e.note: Lop Nur; the old lands of Loulan (Shanshan) lay to its west, and under Wei and Jin the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions was stationed at Haitou.

items.note: 巨野泽，369 年桓温北伐开凿水道三百里，引汶水经此入济。

items.note: 康国（撒马尔罕）、安国（布哈拉）皆依此河。

e.note: Samarkand and Bukhara both depended on this river.

items.note: 乌孙故地，后为高车、突厥游牧之地。

e.note: The old land of the Wusun, later grazing land of the Gaoche and the Turks.

items.note: 天竺西界，法显西行在此渡河。

e.note: The western limit of India, which Faxian crossed on his journey west.

items.note: 笈多王朝的腹地，华氏城、曲女城皆临其流域；法显称“恒水”。

e.note: The heartland of the Gupta dynasty, in whose valley both Pataliputra and Kanyakubja lay; Faxian called it the "Heng River".

items.note: 萨珊都城泰西封在其东岸。

e.note: The Sasanian capital Ctesiphon stood on its east bank.

items.note: 罗马与萨珊长期以其上游一带为界，两国在此反复交战。

e.note: Rome and the Sasanians long had their frontier along its upper course, and fought each other here again and again.

items.note: 东罗马的粮仓埃及依此河而立，亚历山大城在其入海口西侧。

e.note: Egypt, the granary of the Eastern Roman Empire, depended on this river; Alexandria lay to the west of its mouth.

items.note: 《隋书》称阿得水，匈人、保加尔、阿瓦尔先后游牧于其下游。

e.note: Called the Ade River in the Book of Sui; the Huns, the Bulgars and the Avars grazed their herds on its lower course in turn.

items.note: 黑海以北草原上的大河，匈人西进即由此越过阿兰人居地。

e.note: A great river of the steppe north of the Black Sea; it was here that the Huns, moving west, passed over the lands of the Alans.

items.note: 东哥特人的居地，375 年前后为匈人所破。

e.note: Home of the Ostrogoths, broken by the Huns around 375.

items.note: 东罗马在巴尔干的北界，376 年哥特人渡河入境。

e.note: The northern frontier of the Eastern Roman Empire in the Balkans; the Goths crossed it into Roman territory in 376.

items.note: 高加索阿尔巴尼亚、伊比利亚依此河而立。

e.note: Caucasian Albania and Iberia lay along this river.

items.note: 高句丽平壤以北的大河。

e.note: The great river north of Pyongyang in Goguryeo.

items.note: 平壤临其右岸，427 年高句丽长寿王迁都于此。

e.note: Pyongyang lay on its right bank, where King Jangsu of Goguryeo moved his capital in 427.

items.note: 百济都城熊津（475—538）、泗沘（538 年以后）皆临此江。

e.note: Both Baekje capitals, Ungjin (475–538) and Sabi (from 538), lay on this river.

items.note: 药杀水、乌浒水的尾闾，花剌子模在其南。

e.note: The terminal lake of the Jaxartes and the Oxus, with Khwarazm to its south.

items.note: 春秋吴王夫差所开邗沟，自广陵（江都）北至山阳末口入淮，是江淮间的主要水道；东晋时因淤塞改道。南北朝时南军北上、北军南下多经此道。

e.note: The Hangou Canal, dug by King Fuchai of Wu in the Spring and Autumn period, ran north from Guangling (Jiangdu) to Mokou at Shanyang, where it entered the Huai — the main waterway between the Yangtze and the Huai; under the Eastern Jin it was rerouted because of silting. Under the Northern and Southern Dynasties southern armies marching north and northern armies marching south mostly went this way.

items.note: 秦凿，沟通湘水与漓水，是岭南与中原之间的水道。

e.note: Dug under the Qin, it links the Xiang River and the Li River, and was a waterway between Lingnan and the Central Plain.

items.note: 西域南北两道之间的大沙漠，法显称“沙河中多有恶鬼热风，遇则皆死，无一全者”。

e.note: The great desert between the northern and southern routes through the Western Regions; Faxian wrote that "in the river of sand there are many evil demons and hot winds; whoever meets them dies, and not one survives".

items.note: 漠南与漠北之间的戈壁，北魏多次穿越大碛北击柔然。

e.note: The Gobi between the lands south and north of the desert, which the Northern Wei crossed many times to strike at the Rouran.

items.note: 伊朗高原中部的盐漠。

e.note: The salt desert of the central Iranian Plateau.

items.note: 阿拉伯半岛北部的沙漠。

e.note: The desert of the northern Arabian Peninsula.

items.note: 萨珊东部的荒漠。

e.note: The desert of the eastern Sasanian lands.

items.note: 天竺西北，信度河以东的沙漠。

e.note: The desert in northwestern India, east of the Indus.

items.note: 东罗马与萨珊之间，拉赫姆、加萨尼两个阿拉伯王国分居其东西。

e.note: Between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Sasanians, with the two Arab kingdoms of the Ghassanids and the Lakhmids on its western and eastern sides.

items.note: 木鹿以北的沙漠，萨珊与草原诸族之间的屏障。

e.note: The desert north of Merv, a barrier between the Sasanians and the steppe peoples.

items.note: 药杀水与乌浒水之间。

e.note: Between the Jaxartes and the Oxus.

items.note: 阿拉伯半岛南部的“空旷四分之一”。

e.note: The "Empty Quarter" of the southern Arabian Peninsula.

items.note: 祖逖自京口渡江，屯淮阴，317 年进据太丘，319 年攻取谯城，进屯雍丘，收复黄河以南大片土地；321 年病卒于雍丘。

e.note: Zu Ti crossed the Yangtze from Jingkou, camped at Huaiyin, advanced to hold Taiqiu in 317, took the city of Qiao in 319 and advanced to Yongqiu, recovering much of the land south of the Yellow River; he died of illness at Yongqiu in 321.

items.note: 桓温率步骑四万自江陵北上，经南乡、武关入关中，蓝田大捷，进抵灞上；六月白鹿原失利，撤退。

e.note: Huan Wen marched north from Jiangling with forty thousand foot and horse, entered Guanzhong by way of Nanxiang and the Wu Pass, won a great victory at Lantian and advanced to Bashang; after a setback at Bailuyuan in the 6th month he withdrew.

items.note: 桓温自江陵出发，八月在伊水大破姚襄，收复洛阳，修复诸陵后南还。

e.note: Setting out from Jiangling, Huan Wen crushed Yao Xiang at the Yi River in the 8th month, recovered Luoyang, restored the imperial tombs and returned south.

items.note: 桓温率步骑五万自姑孰出发，沿泗水北上，开巨野泽水道入黄河，进至枋头；燕军截断粮道，焚舟陆退，在襄邑遭伏大败。

e.old: Huan Wen's northern expedition against Former Yan
e.note: Huan Wen set out from Gushu with fifty thousand foot and horse, went north along the Si, cut a channel through the Juye Marsh into the Yellow River and advanced to Fangtou; the Yan army cut his supply line, he burned his boats and withdrew overland, and was ambushed and routed at Xiangyi.

items.note: 吕光奉苻坚之命率步骑七万西征，384 年破龟兹，降服西域三十余国；385 年以骆驼二万余头载奇珍东归，九月据姑臧。

e.note: On Fu Jian's orders Lü Guang marched west with seventy thousand foot and horse, took Kucha in 384 and received the submission of more than thirty states of the Western Regions; in 385 he returned east with more than twenty thousand camels laden with rare treasures, and in the 9th month he occupied Guzang.

items.note: 苻坚亲率大军自长安南下，前锋苻融攻克寿阳；淝水大败后苻坚中流矢单骑北逃，经洛阳回到长安。

e.note: Fu Jian marched south from Chang'an at the head of a great army, and his vanguard under Fu Rong took Shouyang; after the defeat at the Fei River Fu Jian, struck by a stray arrow, fled north alone on horseback and returned to Chang'an by way of Luoyang.

items.note: 法显以六十余岁高龄自长安出发，越流沙、葱岭入天竺，游历北、中天竺诸国，在华氏城学梵书三年，又赴狮子国两年，412 年乘商船经耶婆提渡海，在青州长广郡牢山登岸，著《佛国记》。

e.note: Already over sixty, Faxian set out from Chang'an, crossed the flowing sands and the Pamirs into India, traveled through the states of northern and central India, studied Sanskrit at Pataliputra for three years and spent two years in Simhala; in 412 he sailed home on a merchant ship by way of Yavadvipa, came ashore at Mount Lao in Changguang Commandery, Qing Province, and wrote the Record of the Buddhist Kingdoms.

items.note: 刘裕率舟师自淮入泗，在下邳舍舟步进，越大岘山，六月临朐大捷，围广固八月，410 年二月城破。

e.old: Liu Yu's northern expedition against Southern Yan
e.note: Liu Yu led his fleet from the Huai into the Si, left his boats at Xiapi and advanced on foot, crossed the Daxian Mountains, won a great victory at Linqu in the 6th month, besieged Guanggu for eight months, and took it in the 2nd month of 410.

items.note: 刘裕亲率水军自彭城入泗、汴，溯清水入河，以“却月阵”破北魏骑兵，经洛阳西进；王镇恶先已沿渭水攻入长安，九月刘裕入长安，年底东归。

e.old: Liu Yu's northern expedition against Later Qin
e.note: Liu Yu led his fleet in person from Pengcheng into the Si and the Bian, went up the Qing into the Yellow River, broke the Northern Wei cavalry with his "Crescent Formation", and advanced west by way of Luoyang; Wang Zhen'e had already broken into Chang'an along the Wei River, and Liu Yu entered Chang'an in the 9th month and returned east at the end of the year.

items.note: 北魏太武帝自平城南下，渡河解滑台之围，经邹山、彭城直抵长江北岸瓜步，声言渡江；次年正月北还，途中围攻盱眙三十日不下。

e.note: Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei marched south from Pingcheng, crossed the Yellow River to raise the siege of Huatai, and went by way of Mount Zou and Pengcheng straight to Guabu on the north bank of the Yangtze, announcing that he would cross; in the 1st month of the following year he went back north, besieging Xuyi for thirty days on the way without taking it.

items.note: 北魏胡太后派宋云与沙门惠生西行求法，经吐谷浑、鄯善、于阗，翻越葱岭，拜见嚈哒王，至乌苌、乾陀罗，522 年携大乘经论一百七十部回到洛阳。

e.old: Song Yun and Huisheng's journey west
e.note: Empress Dowager Hu of the Northern Wei sent Song Yun and the monk Huisheng west in search of the Dharma; they passed through the Tuyuhun, Shanshan and Khotan, crossed the Pamirs, met the Hephthalite king, reached Udyana and Gandhara, and in 522 returned to Luoyang with 170 Mahayana sutras and treatises.

items.note: 陈庆之以七千白袍军护送元颢北上，自铚县至洛阳，作战四十七次、攻克三十二城，五月入洛；闰六月尔朱荣反攻，全军覆没，陈庆之扮作僧人逃回。

e.note: Chen Qingzhi escorted Yuan Hao north with his seven thousand white-robed troops; from Zhi County to Luoyang he fought forty-seven battles and took thirty-two cities, entering Luoyang in the 5th month; in the intercalary 6th month Erzhu Rong counterattacked, the whole army was wiped out, and Chen Qingzhi escaped disguised as a monk.

items.note: 侯景自寿阳起兵，经谯州、历阳，自采石渡江围建康台城；549 年三月破台城，此后掠三吴，551 年西上攻巴陵失败，552 年被王僧辩、陈霸先击败，东逃海上被杀。

e.note: Hou Jing rose at Shouyang, went by way of Qiaozhou and Liyang, crossed the Yangtze at Caishi and besieged Taicheng in Jiankang; he took Taicheng in the 3rd month of 549 and then plundered the Three Wu; in 551 he went west to attack Baling and failed, and in 552 he was defeated by Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian, fled east by sea and was killed.

items.note: 北周武帝自长安东征，攻克平阳，十二月在平阳城下大破齐后主援军，北上攻取晋阳，577 年正月攻克邺城，追擒齐后主于青州。

e.note: Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou marched east from Chang'an, took Pingyang, crushed the relief army of the Last Ruler of Qi beneath its walls in the 12th month, went north to take Jinyang, took Ye in the 1st month of 577, and pursued and captured the Last Ruler of Qi in Qing Province.

items.note: 东罗马派蔡马库斯回访西突厥，自君士坦丁堡渡黑海，经高加索、伏尔加河下游，至白山（天山）脚下的室点密可汗牙帐，与突厥结盟共抗萨珊。

e.note: The Eastern Roman Empire sent Zemarchus on a return embassy to the Western Turks; from Constantinople he crossed the Black Sea and traveled by way of the Caucasus and the lower Volga to the royal camp of Istämi Qaghan at the foot of the White Mountains (Tian Shan), where an alliance was made with the Turks against the Sasanians.

items.note: 曹操将南匈奴分为五部，散居并州诸郡，刘渊即左部帅之子。

e.old: Five Divisions of the Southern Xiongnu
e.note: Cao Cao divided the Southern Xiongnu into five divisions scattered through the commanderies of Bing Province; Liu Yuan was the son of the commander of the Left Division.

items.note: 匈奴别部，居上党武乡，石勒出身于此，“高鼻多须”。

e.note: A branch of the Xiongnu living at Wuxiang in Shangdang, from whom Shi Le came — "high-nosed and heavily bearded".

items.note: 略阳、天水一带的氐人，杨茂搜的仇池、苻氏的前秦、吕氏的后凉、李氏的成汉（巴氐）皆出于此。

e.note: The Di of the Lüeyang and Tianshui area, from whom came the Yang of Chouchi, the Fu of the Former Qin, the Lü of the Later Liang and the Li of Cheng Han (the Ba Di).

items.note: 匈奴别种，居张掖临松卢水，沮渠蒙逊出身于此。

e.note: A branch of the Xiongnu living on the Lu River at Linsong in Zhangye, from whom Juqu Mengxun came.

items.note: 秃发部等河西鲜卑，270 年代秃发树机能曾大败晋军，后裔建南凉。

e.note: The Tufa and other Hexi Xianbei; in the 270s Tufa Shujineng inflicted great defeats on the Jin army, and their descendants founded the Southern Liang.

items.note: 乞伏部等，居苑川，后裔建西秦。

e.note: The Qifu and others, living at Yuanchuan, whose descendants founded the Western Qin.

items.note: 巴地的板楯蛮（賨人），汉末迁入略阳，李特兄弟即其后。

e.note: The Banshun tribes of Ba (the Cong people), who moved into Lüeyang at the end of the Han; Li Te and his brothers were their descendants.

items.note: 敕勒南迁的一支，居中山、河内，翟斌、翟辽先后起兵，建立翟魏。

e.note: A branch of the Chile that moved south, living in Zhongshan and Henei; Zhai Bin and Zhai Liao rose in turn and founded Zhai Wei.

items.note: 曹操北征后乌桓散居塞内，西晋时仍以突骑著称，王浚、刘琨皆用其兵。

e.note: After Cao Cao's northern campaign the Wuhuan lived scattered inside the frontier; under the Western Jin they were still famous as shock cavalry, used by both Wang Jun and Liu Kun.

items.note: 江南山地的土著，孙吴屡次征讨，西晋时多已编户。

e.mod: hill country of Zhejiang and Anhui
e.note: The native peoples of the southern hill country, repeatedly campaigned against by Sun Wu; by Western Jin times most had been registered as subjects.

items.note: 荆、雍、豫三州山谷间的“诸蛮”，南北朝时依违两国之间，时有起事。

e.note: The "Man tribes" of the mountain valleys of Jing, Yong and Yu provinces, who under the Northern and Southern Dynasties wavered between the two sides and rose from time to time.

items.note: 344 年前后自南中大量北迁入蜀，散居梁、益二州山谷，成为南北朝时期巴蜀的重要人群。

e.note: Around 344 they moved north from Nanzhong into Shu in great numbers and settled in the mountain valleys of Liang and Yi provinces, becoming an important people of Ba-Shu under the Northern and Southern Dynasties.

items.note: 岭南土著，以高凉冼氏为首领；冼夫人历梁、陈、隋三朝，保境安民。

e.note: The native people of Lingnan, led by the Xian clan of Gaoliang; Lady Xian served Liang, Chen and Sui in turn, keeping her territory secure and its people at peace.

items.note: 武陵山区的蛮族，散居五溪之间。

e.note: Tribes of the Wuling mountain region, scattered among the Five Streams.

items.note: 南中诸族，与南中大姓杂处。

e.note: Peoples of Nanzhong, living among the great clans of Nanzhong.

items.note: 又称山胡、步落稽，匈奴后裔与诸族融合而成，居离石以西、安定以东的山谷，北朝时屡屡起事。

e.note: Also called Shanhu (Mountain Hu) or Buluoji, formed from descendants of the Xiongnu mixed with other peoples; they lived in the mountain valleys west of Lishi and east of Anding, and rose repeatedly under the Northern Dynasties.

items.note: 居北秀容川的契胡部落，世以畜牧为业，尔朱荣出身于此。

e.note: A Qihu tribe living in the Northern Xiurong valley, herders by tradition, from whom Erzhu Rong came.

items.note: 429 年北魏大破高车，徙其数十万落于漠南，东至濡源、西暨五原阴山，北朝民歌《敕勒歌》即咏其地。

e.mod: north of the Yin Mountains, Inner Mongolia
e.note: In 429 the Northern Wei crushed the Gaoche and moved several hundred thousand of their tents to the land south of the Gobi, from the source of the Nuan in the east to Wuyuan and the Yin Mountains in the west; the Northern Dynasties folk song "Song of the Chile" celebrates that land.

items.note: 居金山之阳，为柔然锻奴，546 年土门破铁勒，552 年大破柔然建国。

e.note: Living on the southern side of the Altai, they worked iron as servants of the Rouran; in 546 Tumen crushed the Tiele, and in 552 he crushed the Rouran and founded his state.

items.note: 高车（敕勒）诸部在突厥兴起后通称铁勒，役属突厥。

e.note: After the rise of the Turks the Gaoche (Chile) tribes were generally called Tiele, and were subjects of the Turks.

items.note: 汉代称坚昆，北朝称结骨、契骨，“人皆长大，赤发、皙面、绿瞳”。

e.note: Called Jiankun in Han times and Jiegu or Qigu under the Northern Dynasties; "the people are all tall, with red hair, white faces and green eyes".

items.note: 230 年孙权派卫温、诸葛直率万人浮海至夷洲，三国至隋称夷洲、流求。

e.note: In 230 Sun Quan sent Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi with ten thousand men across the sea to Yizhou; from the Three Kingdoms to the Sui it was called Yizhou or Liuqiu.

items.note: 倭王武 478 年上表宋顺帝，称其先祖“东征毛人五十五国”。

e.note: In 478 King Bu of Wa sent a memorial to Emperor Shun of Song saying that his ancestors had "conquered fifty-five countries of the Emishi in the east".

items.note: 6 世纪起见于东罗马史籍，自多瑙河以北南下袭扰巴尔干。

e.note: Recorded in Eastern Roman histories from the 6th century, they came south from beyond the Danube to raid the Balkans.
